- [x] #197 Do option 1 first: verify the codegen ownership path before applying the fix.  This is very likely the right fix, but because pool registration changes ownership/lifetime semantics globally, please confirm the existing `take` behavior first.  Specifically verify:  1. `let s: String = a + b`    The concat result must be detached from the string pool with `rae_string_pool_take(...)`, so it survives statement-scope flush and is later dropped as local owned String.  2. `ret a + b`    The return epilogue must detach the concat result with `rae_string_pool_take(...)`, so it survives function cleanup/flush.  3. `foo(a + b)` where `foo` takes `view String`    The concat result should remain pool-owned and be flushed after the statement.  4. Nested concat / int-to-string:    `"x" + i.toString()` should not leak intermediate concat or int_to_str results.  If those ownership paths are already correct, apply the small fix:  - register `rae_ext_rae_str_concat` results with the string pool - register `rae_str_from_buf_impl` results with the string pool - register `rae_str_from_cstr_impl` results if it creates owned heap strings  Then run: - full compiler tests - all examples - 20K Compiled mobile UI stress with `RAE_MEM_STATS=1`  Success criteria: - concat outstanding goes to ~0 - int_to_str outstanding goes to ~0 - no double-free regressions - mobile UI stress slope drops close to zero  Do not broaden the patch unless verification shows missing `pool_take` codegen.

The pool_take codegen IS firing on concat RHS (verified in c_stmt.c:438/528/596) so the result IS removed from the pool — but the downstream owner (struct field assignment, list element add, ret-from-helper returning String, etc.) never frees it at its own scope exit. Diagnose by: (a) running mobile UI stress at 5K with extra logging from inside rae_mem_str_untag tracking which call path frees the few concats that DO get freed; (b) inspecting generated C for one buildScreenWorld helper to see whether `component.style = concat(...)` lowers to a path that loses the str_free at component drop; (c) check whether Layer 5 synth'd drop is missing String fields. Likely outcome: cascade-drop gap for struct field reassign OR a List<String>.add path that doesn't tag the element as owned.

- [x] #202 Compiler fix: `own String` param double-free. Caller-side codegen emits `rae_string_drop(&src); content = pool_take(call_result)` after invoking a function with `content: own String` param, while the callee also drops the param at function exit → "POINTER_BEING_FREED_WAS_NOT_ALLOCATED" abort. - [x] #203 Compiler/stdlib fix: `lib/string.replace` returns aliasing String. The function has `if old.length() is 0 { ret this }` and the split+join path also produces a String that, in some shapes, ends up sharing storage with `this` (or with whatever was assigned to the concat accumulator most recently). Visible symptom: a long pipeline of `r = r.replace(...).replace(...); ret r` returned values that, when subsequently embedded into another concat chain, contained bytes from the OUTER accumulator. Either make `ret this` deep-copy, or audit the split+join branches for alias return.

- [x] #333 Depth/normal/velocity prepass; DROP MSAA. Single-sampled Depth32Float + a real normal target (not depth-reconstructed — reconstruction is wrong exactly at the edges where AO/GI matter) + rg16f velocity. Dropping MSAA is what makes depth sampleable (WebGPU guarantees no depth resolve), which unblocks SSAO, GI gathering, SSR and volumetrics in one move. Metaballs move INTO the prepass (raymarch writes frag_depth + normal) so implicit and triangle geometry unify for shading/AO/GI/TAA instead of every technique special-casing them. DONE: single-sampled Depth32Float (stored, sampleable) + rgba16f real world normals + rg16f velocity, MRT from both the raster and SDF passes so implicit and triangle geometry are indistinguishable downstream. MSAA removed.
- [x] #334 HDR scene colour + tonemap as a pass — rgba16f scene target; move the ACES tonemap OUT of the material uber-shader into its own pass; UI composites in LDR after tonemap. This is a prerequisite, not polish: accumulating GI on tonemapped values is mathematically wrong (light does not add after a nonlinear curve), so any indirect lighting built on the current pipeline would be incorrect regardless of algorithm quality. DONE: rgba16f linear HDR scene target; ACES+exposure+gamma moved out of both material shaders into a dedicated tonemap pass that is the only writer of the LDR offscreen; UI composites after it in display space.
- [x] #335 TAA — jittered projection (Halton 2,3 sub-pixel offset in mat4Perspective, removed before reprojection maths), motion vectors, persistent rgba16f history, neighbourhood/variance clamping. Not just antialiasing: jitter+history+reprojection are the same temporal substrate GI accumulation needs, so this is shared infrastructure. Known costs to manage: ghosting on disocclusion, softening, care with thin geometry. Depends on #336. DONE: Halton(2,3) clip-space jitter (velocity computed from UNJITTERED positions), per-object motion vectors via a prevModel matrix per draw, ping-ponged rgba16f history, neighbourhood-clamped luminance-weighted resolve on linear HDR before tonemap. taaColor is the graph’s first Persistent resource. RAE_NO_TAA=1 opts out; captures stay deterministic.

Neither exists today. Small change to the scene model, blocks two later items. GPU wiring for prev-model matrices landed with #335.
- [x] #337 SSAO — DONE: horizon-search AO with a 32-bit VISIBILITY BITMASK per slice (GTAO, Jimenez 2016 + Jover 2023) rather than hemisphere sampling — a horizon search integrates a whole angular sector per sample so it converges with far fewer taps, and the bitmask records each occluded sector independently instead of guessing what is behind an occluder, which is what removes GTAO's thin-geometry over-darkening. Sector boundaries are uniform in SIN so a plain popcount approximates the cosine-weighted integral (no weight table, no arccos inner loop). Half-res generation + depth-weighted 3x3 bilateral upsample; contact-scale radius by design so it stays valid alongside #339 GI; interleaved-gradient noise rotates the basis per pixel and per frame so TAA integrates the samples. Applied to the INDIRECT term only — the scene pass now writes ambient to its own MRT attachment (raster AND SDF, so both geometry kinds split identically) and the composite adds ambient*AO back into hdrColor as a graph read-modify-write. One quality knob: `RAE_SSAO_QUALITY=mobile|low|desktop|high` (2x4 .. 4x8 slices x steps); plus RAE_SSAO_RADIUS, RAE_NO_SSAO, RAE_SSAO_DEBUG (raw AO view). KNOWN: faint stipple remains on mid-tones at half-res; a wider spatial denoise or a dedicated AO-history TAA channel would be the next step.
- [x] #343 COMPILER BUG — adding an INTERPOLATED string to a `List(String)` corrupts the element and double-frees on teardown (SIGABRT). Minimal repro: `let m: String = "gamma"` then `plain.add(value: "{m}")` into a `List(String)` reads back as garbage/empty and aborts at exit; `add(value: m)` (plain variable) and `add(value: "literal")` both work. Not struct-related — reproduces with a bare local List. Almost certainly the string pool: an interpolated string is pool-registered/owned, `List.add` stores the pointer without taking ownership, the pool flush frees it, leaving a dangling element and a second free at list drop. Worked around in lib/rendergraph.rae by storing names without interpolation; the workaround is commented at the call site so it is not "cleaned up" later. Related to the known interp-`{...}` residual-leak note. FIXED: root cause was a missing AST_EXPR_INTERP case in infer_expr_type_ref, which returned NULL and so silently disabled the pool_take wrap in c_call.c that already existed for exactly this. Regression test 554 covers all five paths through that argument slot.

- [x] #346 Metaball clusters with per-ball colour blending (110) — SdfPrimitive gained `cluster` and `smoothing`; only primitives sharing a cluster fuse, and stickiness is per cluster. Albedo is per PRIMITIVE: the weight that fuses two distances also mixes their colours, so a cluster can hold a gradient. 110 ships three deliberately contrasting clusters (blue k0.62, near-black obsidian k0.30 slow, emissive ember k1.15 fast) plus periodic breakaway droplets. Found and fixed en route: one shared SDF buffer set cannot serve multiple draws per frame — wgpuQueueWriteBuffer applies at submit, so every cluster rendered the last one's data.

Drawn directly through gpu2d rather than as ECS entities so a diagnostic cannot perturb the layout/component tables it is meant to observe, and the panel width is a window fraction so no per-frame text measuring. Anchored bottom-left in 110, top-left in 106 (configurable margins clear a status bar). `revision` lets a change-driven loop treat a new line as a reason to redraw. First consumer: `nextReloadGeneration()` in lib/hot_reload.rae logs "hot reload N" at startup, so a reload that silently failed to relaunch is distinguishable from one that changed nothing.
- [x] #348 110 state survives hot reload — selected scene, pause/speed/debug toggles and the FULL camera (orbit-vs-WASD mode, yaw/pitch, distance, free position, target) persist through `lib/hot_reload.rae`'s state file. Saved on CHANGE and throttled to 4/sec (110 does not watch for a reload signal, so an exit-only save would lose everything to a hard kill; one file write per frame during a camera drag would be exactly the hidden cost this app measures), plus a final flush on clean exit. New app-scoped helpers `readHotReloadStateFor`/`writeHotReloadStateFor` keep it out of `state.json`, which belongs to whichever app's schema wrote it (106 stores playback state there). Payload is one version-tagged line of numbers so a stale/corrupt/newer snapshot degrades to a clean start rather than half-applying a camera — verified: garbage, truncated, future-version and empty all boot at defaults without crashing.
- [x] #349 COMPILER BUG — FIXED: a CHAINED call on a generic method's result mis-resolved silently. `parts.at(i).toInt()` on a `List(String)` bound to a same-named overload for another receiver type (List2Int.length), surfacing as an inscrutable C type error rather than an overload diagnostic. Cause: sema built the receiver type-ref for `infer_generic_args` from the INSTANTIATED struct's mangled name (`List_String`) while a generic method's param is written against the template (`view List(T)`), so inference bailed and the call got neither decl_link nor resolved_type — leaving the next link in the chain resolving against nothing. Fixed in the BACKEND's `infer_expr_type_ref` METHOD_CALL case, NOT sema's overload selection: three attempts there each regressed the same 8 generic-container tests (412/413/414/415/420/423/440/442) because changing which candidate is chosen perturbs ECS/StringMap resolution. The fix recovers the callee by name+receiver base type when decl_link is NULL, then substitutes the receiver's generic arg for a returned type param POSITIONALLY (slot of the param in the `this` type, so a method declaring its type params in a different order than the struct still maps correctly). Test 555; 110's `string.toInt(this: ...)` workaround removed.
- [x] #351 READINESS TRACK A0 — design doc for fixed-size value aggregates + checked ownership transfer, co-designed. The two foundations from `rae/docs/language-readiness-for-renderer.md` (§3, §4, Track A). Settle on paper BEFORE implementing: spelling of `[N]T` (const-expression N?), value semantics (trivially copyable when T is primitive, no cascade-drop), indexing bounds policy (checked debug / unchecked release?), whether it lowers to a distinct type kind or a compile-time-length Buffer; AND the container-boundary ownership rules — most importantly whether passing a non-owned value to an `own T` parameter becomes a COMPILE ERROR instead of a silent alias/double-free (the root of the log_overlay, List(Struct) deep-copy and #225 hazards). Deliverable: a short design doc + the test list for #353. Do not write compiler code under this item.
- [x] #352 READINESS TRACK A1 — implement fixed-size value aggregates per #351: parser, sema, C backend lowering to a plain C array/struct by value, ownership integration, drop semantics for heap-element T. Acceptance: a `[16]Float` embeds in a struct, passes by value, stores in List elements, and a transform microbench shows ZERO allocations — but per Track B the REAL exit criterion lives in #356, not here. DONE as `Array(T, cap: N)` (spelling revised in #351 rev 2/3) across four slices: (1) compile-time value generic arguments via an interned TYPE_CONST_INT, folded through sema's existing const_eval; (2) TYPE_ARRAY lowering to `struct { T v[N]; }` — never a bare C array, which would decay to a pointer and reintroduce aliasing — plus indexing and compile-time constant bounds checks; (3) drops exactly when the element type does, per-element loop for Array(String), ZERO drop code for Array(Float); (4) List(Mat4) with verified value-copy into the container. 194 compiler cases + 70 examples green. Remaining gap filed as #361.
- [x] #354 READINESS TRACK A3 — value math types on top of #352: `Vec2`, `Vec4`, `Quat`, `Mat4`, `Mat3x4` as allocation-free value types in lib (Vec3 exists; keep its API shape). Mat3x4 matters: affine transforms need no fourth row and the reference engine ships mat3x4 across its render boundary for 25% less transform traffic. Port `lib/math3d.rae` OFF List(Float) as a consequence — note per the doc this port is NOT the exit criterion, #356 is. DONE: Mat4 = Array(Float, cap: 16) in a struct, Mat3x4 with converters both ways, and Vec2/Vec4/Quat as named-field structs (matching Vec3 — Array is for large homogeneous counts, not 4 components, so #361 does not block this). mat4Mul and modelMatrix verified allocation-free in the emitted C. gpu3d stages through two process-lifetime scratch lists at the extern boundary; retyping the externs to `view Mat4` is a deliberate follow-up. Filed #362 (cross-module symbol collision) hit on the way.
- [x] #355 READINESS TRACK C — cheap unblocking language items, safe to do anytime/in parallel: (a) `continue`/`break` (only subtlety: interaction with defer + scope-exit drops), (b) `List.removeLast()`/`truncate(len)`/`removeAt(i)` running element drop via the existing rae_ext_rae_buf_drop_at path, (c) `popcount`/`leadingZeros`/`trailingZeros` intrinsics. - [x] #360 Compiler: `rae format` SIGSEGVs on ANY module-level binding — `let`, `var` AND `const` (my original note claiming let/var were unaffected was wrong; all three share AST_DECL_GLOBAL_LET). pp_print_decl had no case for that kind, so it fell through to pp_print_func_decl and read func fields out of a let union. - [x] #361 Compiler: a raw `Array(T, cap: N)` in a generic type-argument slot (`createList(Array(Float, cap: 4), cap: 2)`) does not resolve — type params live outside `fd->params`, so the call never matches the overload, and it fails as a wall of C compiler errors instead of a Rae diagnostic. Consequence of #352's type-doubles-as-constructor rule. Options: (a) classify a call argument as a type when it fills a `T: type` slot, (b) require a named wrapper type (works today, what the renderer wants anyway), or (c) type aliases `type Vec4 = Array(Float, cap: 4)` — which also gives #354's math types their natural spelling. Add a proper diagnostic either way.
- [x] #362 Compiler: two functions in DIFFERENT modules with the same name, arity and parameter types mangle to the same C symbol — `vec4.create(x,y,z,w)` and `quat.create(x,y,z,w)` collided as `rae_create_rae_View_Float_x4` ("conflicting types"). The mangler includes neither the module nor the return type. Worked around in #354 by renaming quat's to `fromXYZW`, but this will keep biting as lib/ grows value types with parallel APIs, and it silently constrains every module to globally-unique signatures. Fix: include the defining module in the mangled symbol. DONE: defined functions mangle as rae_<module>_<name>_<params>, extending the pattern namespaced stdlib externs already used. Externs untouched (they name real C entry points); the entry/project module has no module_name so `main` and single-file programs are unchanged. quat.create restored. 229 cases + 70 examples green.
- [x] #363 Compiler: the own-argument rule (#353) cannot see generic-container method calls — `list.add(value: someViewParam)`, the log_overlay shape it was designed around. Sema never binds those calls to a decl (`decl_link` is NULL), the same structural limitation that forced #349's fix into the backend; the method-table, generic-overload and UFCS-rewrite paths were all hooked and none see them. Two routes: (a) resolve generic methods in sema — the work that regressed eight tests during #349 — or (b) a second check in c_call.c where the callee IS resolved, trading the doc's "sema runs on all paths" rationale for actually catching the main hazard. DONE via (b): narrow backend check (bare view/mod into `own`), `own x` as the explicit per-argument escape, and NO stdlib exemption — which found four real latent double-frees in lib/string.rae, lib/rendergraph.rae (x2) and 106.
- [x] #382 Shadows M1 — cascaded shadow map, minimum viable, per `rae/docs/shadow-system-design.md` §8.1: 3 ortho cascades for the sun, TEXEL-SNAPPED in world space (the anti-shimmer rule, and the thing that reads as "pixelation" if omitted), fitted to frustum-slice bounding spheres so resolution does not change with camera yaw, normal-offset bias rather than depth bias alone, one stochastic sample per pixel at a fixed radius, depth-aware spatial denoise, resolved into a full-res r8unorm shadowMask that multiplies DIRECT light only. - [x] #384 Shadows M3 — variable penumbra and temporal denoise (design doc §3 A2/A3): blocker search sets the sample disc radius from the sun's true 0.53 degree angular diameter, and the mask accumulates through the existing TAA history plus the shared depth-aware blur from #372. Needs shadow-specific history rejection on mask delta; the colour clamp alone ghosts on moving occluders.

- [x] #393 DEFERRED MIGRATION — 110 and 113 both migrated and proven. Move examples 110 and 113 onto renderer_deferred once #387-#392 are all done. - [x] #396 DEFERRED TOON SHADING mode, plus a persistent style toggle in example 113. Deferred is the right place for it: the G-buffer already stores surface attributes independent of how they are lit, so a shading STYLE is a different read of the same buffer rather than a different set of material shaders — which is exactly the separation the forward path could not offer. Two ways in, and the choice matters: (a) a PER-MATERIAL mode, using the one free slot in the G-buffer's 2-bit material_mode field (LIT=0, EMISSIVE=1/3, UNLIT=2/3 are taken; 3/3 is free), so toon and PBR objects can coexist in one frame; or (b) a WHOLE-FRAME lighting-pass switch via a uniform, which is one branch and no G-buffer change but cannot mix styles. Prefer (a) — it costs no extra bits and the mixed case is the interesting one. Toon itself: quantise NdotL into bands, keep the shadow mask multiplying direct only (§5 still holds — a banded shadow edge must come from quantising the LIGHT, not from quantising the mask), specular as a hard thresholded highlight, and a rim term. NO edge outlines in this task: they need a depth/normal discontinuity pass and are their own increment. Example 113 gets a style toggle button in its control panel, and the choice must survive a hot reload — it goes in the #377 state line, which means bumping state113Version.
- [x] #397 Deferred TAA sub-pixel JITTER, the missing half of #390. Without it TAA is a temporal blur rather than antialiasing: every frame samples the same point inside each pixel, so accumulating frames adds no new information and only risks ghosting. Add a Halton(2,3) clip-space offset to the G-buffer frame uniform and apply it AFTER o.clipNow is captured — motion must stay unjittered or every static pixel appears to move. The forward path does exactly this in runtime_gpu3d.c; the constants and the sequence can be lifted directly.
- [x] #398 Optimise the metaball shadow caster (#392 follow-up). It works but costs: each cluster is a FULLSCREEN raymarch per cascade, so example 110 runs 3 clusters x 3 cascades = 9 full 2048x2048 marches per frame and drops from ~23 to ~16 fps. Two obvious bounds, in order of value: (a) restrict each cluster to the screen extent of its bounding sphere projected into the cascade, instead of a fullscreen triangle — most of a 2048 map is empty for a 2-metre blob; (b) skip distant cascades for small clusters, since a blob smaller than a few far-cascade texels contributes nothing. Neither changes the image, so both are verifiable by byte-comparing a headless screenshot before and after.

- [x] #442 [opt/alias arc 1/6] Implement `opt view T` / `opt mod T` per spec 4.1: permitted in parameters, return types and local bindings, bound with `=>`, excluded from type members by 4.3. Today the Compiled target accepts them and emits C that will not build, while the frozen VM rejects them outright (vm_compiler.c, "opt view/mod not allowed") — that rejection must go, it enforces a rule the spec no longer has. Tests 382_reject_opt_alias and 385_reject_opt_alias_return pin the removed rule and must be retired or inverted in the same change
- [x] #443 [opt/alias arc 2/6] `=>` onto a produced value must materialise. Per spec 2.3, `let a: view T => f()` is semantically valid whether or not f returns a place; the implementation must give the value storage for the binding's lifetime. Today accepted and emits broken C (same for `list.at(index: 0)`). Functions returning `view T` / `mod T` already work and must keep working
- [x] #444 [opt/alias arc 3/6] Fix `view`/`mod` locals of primitive type. `let v: view Int => x` binds, but reading it back (`let r: Int = v`) or interpolating it emits broken C — rae_View_Int64 passed where int64_t/rae_String is expected. Struct views already work
- [x] #445 [opt/alias arc 4/6] Enforce the generalised 2.2 rule: `=>` is REQUIRED, not merely permitted, whenever the target type contains `view` or `mod` at any level — including `opt view T` / `opt mod T`. This is what stops `=` ever producing a shared handle instead of an independent value. Needs a diagnostic on `let x: opt view T = …`
- [x] #446 [opt/alias arc 5/6] Implement `if let` per spec 4.2: `if let x: view T => optExpr` / `if let x: mod T => optExpr`, binding scoped to the if-branch, bind-once, `=` REJECTED with a diagnostic citing 2.3. Narrows `opt T`, `opt view T` and `opt mod T`. Depends on 2/6 and 3/6, since the common right-hand side is a call like `map.get(k:)`
- [x] #447 [opt/alias arc 6/6] Two loose ends: the spec/implementation divergence on assignment through a `let`-bound mod alias (spec 2.2's example says legal, the compiler demands `var`), and `is some`, which parses but fails with "use of undeclared identifier 'some'" — implement it as the mirror of `is none` or remove it. - [x] #448 Pre-existing before the opt/alias arc and still failing: 338_reject_ref_to_local and 339_reject_ref_to_temporary. - [x] #456 Spec 2.3.1: Rae diagnostic for `let t: T = <view/mod-returning call>` — currently emits broken C (initializing rae_Track with const rae_Track*). - [x] #457 Spec 4.2 (revised again — construct-ownership rule WITHDRAWN): `if let` applies the 2.3.1 matrix unchanged. - [x] #458 Semantic liveness tests per the observable-behavior philosophy: pin (a) a `view T` binding observes mutations made through the original while the view is alive, and (b) writes through a `mod T` binding are visible in the original. Both hold today (probed) but nothing pins them; a future 'optimise views to copies' change must fail these tests unless it proves no observable change — done: pinned in test 612 (view sees mutation, mod write-back), plus param-alias liveness
- [x] #459 Writes through a `view` binding must be REJECTED — currently ACCEPTED and they write through to the original (probe: `let v: view Track => t; v.value = 42` mutates t). - [x] #511 BUG (shadows): in 114 (and any deferred scene) directional shadows VANISH while the sun is up (~06:45–17:12) and only appear when the sun is below the horizon — inverted. Root cause is the cascade depth-range fit in lib/shadow3d.rae (~line 165-193): the light view is a PURE ROTATION anchored at the world origin (eye=0), and the ortho near/far come from `centreLs.z` (scene centre transformed into light space) as zNear=-centreLs.z-radius-backExtent, zFar=-centreLs.z+radius. When the sun is HIGH the light travels DOWNWARD, so the origin-anchored down-looking light camera has the scene centre BEHIND it → centreLs.z > 0 → both z values go negative → the `if zNear < 0.01 { zNear = 0.01 }` clamp pins near but leaves far possibly < near → degenerate/empty ortho depth range → the cascade renders nothing → no shadows. When the sun is DOWN the light points up, the centre is in front, the range is valid, so shadows appear (wrongly, at night). FIX (needs visual verification): make the depth range enclose the centre regardless of the sign of centreLs.z — e.g. anchor the light eye along the light axis behind the centre (eye = centre - light*backDist) so depth is always positive, OR shift near/far together to keep near>=0.01 AND far>near AND still bracket [centreLs.z-radius, centreLs.z+radius]. Verify shadows are present and correct across a full day cycle (noon included) in 114/110, and that texel-snapping (test 579) still holds. Not a #504 migration item; a standalone correctness fix.

- [x] #623 COMPILER: break / continue in `loop` (docs/match-and-sum-types.md Proposal A). Reuse the existing early-`ret` ownership-drop machinery (compiler/src/ownership.c): `break` drops `own` values in scopes up to the loop then exits; `continue` drops the current iteration's `own` values then jumps to next iteration. Reverse-construction drop order, same as scope exit. Removes `var done` flag-guard patterns.

- [x] #626 COMPILER BUG: a `let` of an OWNED value inside a `match case` mis-scopes its drop. ## Archived 2026-08-27 (opt/reference/container semantics epic #641–#661)

- [x] #641 Inline representation for `opt T` (drop the RaeAny box). Motivation: `opt T` for a non-reference value type is realized as a heap-boxed `RaeAny` (malloc(sizeof(payload)) + copy + rae_any_owned_ptr, emitted around compiler/src/c_stmt.c:308-338; C type RaeAny at c_backend.c:603). Only the `if let` peepholes on `at`/`viewAt`/`modAt` avoid the malloc, and they are keyed on library function-name strings (emit_list_if_let, c_stmt.c:32-120), so every new accessor is another shape to recognize and every unrecognized shape is a heap cliff (the §8 bug); the representation is the root cause, the peepholes treat a symptom. Scope: lower `opt T` for non-reference `T` to a per-type monomorphized `struct rae_opt_T { bool has; T value; }` (the mechanism `List(T)` already uses); `opt T` needs a drop only if `T` does (type_needs_cascade_drop); reserve `RaeAny` for `Any` only. NOTE (verified, corrects the report): `opt view T`/`opt mod T` are ALREADY plain 8-byte nullable reference wrappers (null .ptr = none, c_backend.c:596-603) — they are NOT boxed and need NO change; this task is only about `opt T` for non-reference T. Then delete the name-keyed `at`/`viewAt`/`modAt` peepholes, or demote them to a pure optimization behind a test proving the generated C is equivalent without them, so the accessors become small ordinary functions the C compiler inlines. Acceptance: no `malloc` in generated C for any call shape of `at`/`viewAt`/`modAt`, including `let maybe: opt Particle = particles.at(index: index)` stored and passed to another function; a user function returning `opt Vec3` produces no heap traffic; the report's layout table still holds; peephole code removed or demoted with the equivalence test in place. Deps: none required; if done after #645 the peephole removal is cleaner; blocks the peephole-removal half of #644. DONE 2026-08-26: struct/aggregate `opt T` now lowers to a monomorphized `struct rae_opt_<T>{ rae_Bool has; T value; }` (0 malloc in emitted C for `at`/`viewAt`/`modAt` and for a user `ret opt Vec3`; `opt Vec3`→`struct rae_opt_rae_Vec3{has,value}` verified; case suite 317/0). Scoped to aggregate payloads: scalar/String `opt` stay on the already-malloc-free `RaeAny` union, and the `at`/`viewAt`/`modAt` peephole is kept as a pure optimization. Follow-ups filed: #651 (finish "RaeAny for Any only" — move scalar/String opt off the union), #652 (pre-existing generic-`get`/`at` double-free on heap-owning struct payloads, surfaced here).
- [x] #642 `opt T` to `T` direct assignment is a sema error for every `T`. Motivation: `let particle: Particle = particles.at(index: index)` emits non-compiling C (a RaeAny box assigned into a struct-typed C variable; emit_opt_unbox_suffix, c_call.c:21-59, emits no suffix for struct payloads), while `let count: Int = list.at(index: index)` does NOT trap on none — the scalar path unconditionally reads the union (.as.i/.as.f/...) so a `none` silently yields zero with no diagnostic (this corrects the report's "auto-unwraps trivially": it is a silent-zero bug, not benign). Two different wrong behaviors for one situation. Scope: one rule — assigning `opt T` to a non-optional binding requires `if let`, a default-value operator, or an explicit unwrap that panics; Rae has no default/unwrap operator yet, so PROPOSE the syntax in this task rather than inventing it during implementation (candidates to decide in review: `list.at(index: index) else 0` for a default, `list.at(index: index)!` for a panicking unwrap); the error message must name the fix. Acceptance: scalar and struct forms produce the same sema error with the same message; the silent-zero scalar path is gone; tests for both forms; the report's §8 bug entry closed. Deps: independent of #641. DECISION 2026-08-26 (approved): NO new language features (no `!`, no `else`, no `[]`, no trap/panic, no `.first()`/`.last()`, no enumerate loop). Rule: every optional ends in `if let`; the else branch returns a value the PROGRAMMER wrote, never a compiler-invented one. Investigation (2 classifiers + Array/Buffer probe): the ~299 grep lines are ~48–265 real sites collapsing to ~15–30 distinct changes; 34 are false positives (`Task.get()` joins + already-`opt` map gets — SKIP), dominated by the `ResolvedTheme` struct-of-arrays. Migration (batched by file, in order): (1) parallel-lists-by-key (ResolvedTheme, frames.rae, gltf channel SoA, legacy textures) → `StringMap` or a `List` of `{name,value}` structs iterated with `loop`+`view` where order matters — `themeSpaceValue` → one `if let` on `StringMap.get(key:)` + `ret fallback`; (2) fixed-size lists unpacked by constant index (`quadTile`, window_geometry parts, color parts, nowPlayingTimes) → a struct returned by value; (3) flat-buffer samplers (`mesh3d`, `gltf_skin`, `compress/*`, tetris grids, json cursor, gltf palette) → keep the data a `List`, one helper per buffer doing `copyAt` in `if let` with an explicit programmer fallback in else (e.g. `ret 0.0`), callers keep clamping; (4) loop-by-counter read-only → range `loop` with `view` (`mod` where the body mutates); (5) genuinely optional + the misc guarded-first/last/single-char reads → `if let` with an explicit else value. Motivation: requiring `copy` on every binding would be noise on `Int`/`Float`/`Vec2` and would duplicate the `=` vs `=>` distinction; types where `type_needs_cascade_drop` is true own heap, so copying them is a deep copy with allocation and should be spelled out. Scope: (1) determine what happens today when a struct that owns a `List` is bound by value (`let copyOfOwner: Owner = owner`): move, deep copy, or shallow copy with a later double free; (2) design: require `copy` in the binding for cascade-drop types, implicit copy for everything else, and give `copy` real deep-copy codegen; (3) file implementation as a follow-up. Deps: relates to #641 (drop generation). DONE 2026-08-27 — investigation (emitted C): (1) binding a cascade-drop struct by value (`let x: Owner = owner`) is ALREADY an implicit DEEP copy (`rae_deep_copy_<T>`), unconditional (even on a dead/last-use source — no move optimization); it is SAFE — independent heaps, both dropped, no double-free/leak (RAE_MEM_STATS outstanding=0). NOT a shallow copy. (2) `copy T` and `own T` LOCAL bindings emit the SAME deep copy as bare `T` — `is_copy`/`is_own` are annotation-only for locals (ast.h:38), affecting only parameter-passing codegen. (3) Non-cascade-drop types (Point/Vec2/Particle-no-heap) are a plain `rae_T b = a;` struct copy — no deep copy, no allocation. CORRECTION to premise: the deep-copy codegen already exists AND bare `T` already uses it; there is no missing codegen and no shallow-copy double-free — the gap is a SEMANTIC REQUIREMENT (nothing forces `copy`, so the heap allocation is hidden). Design note docs/copy-mode-cascade-drop.md: RECOMMEND requiring `copy` on cascade-drop value bindings (bare → sema error; write `copy T` to deep-copy or `view`/`mod` to alias — mirrors #643 copyAt/viewAt/modAt and #644 `=`/`=>`), non-cascade-drop keep implicit copy. HONEST CAVEAT recorded: with no move-of-locals, `copy` deep-copies exactly as the implicit bind does today, so the payoff is explicitness/auditability, NOT perf or correctness; the higher-value alternative is move-on-last-use for the bare case (separate, larger). Follow-up + decision point filed as #659.

- [x] #657 Clean "no method on receiver" diagnostic for generic UFCS misresolution. Surfaced during #643: calling a method that doesn't exist on the receiver (e.g. `someList.at(index: 0)` after `at` was removed from `List`) does NOT produce a clean sema error — the generic UFCS matcher instead binds it to a same-named function on a DIFFERENT type (e.g. `String.at`, or the generic `List.copyAt`/`List2.get`), emitting confusing C-level type errors (`initializing 'RaeAny' with int64`, `rae_core_copyAt_rae_List_rae_T_...` undeclared) at the generated-C line instead of the .rae call site. Scope: when UFCS/method resolution finds a candidate whose receiver type doesn't actually match, reject it and emit a sema error naming the receiver type and method ("no method `at` on `List(Int)`; did you mean `copyAt`?"). Acceptance: a `list.at(index:)` (or any wrong-receiver method) errors at the .rae site with a clear message, not a downstream C error. Deps: none. DONE 2026-08-27 — KEY FINDING: sema's method matching intentionally leaves many VALID calls unresolved (a SPECIALIZED receiver `List_int64_t` does not match a method's generic template `this: mod List(T)`), so the C backend is the real resolver; erroring on every unresolved method call flags valid code (`add`, etc.). Fix (sema.c METHOD_CALL, after all resolution paths): when a call is unresolved AND a same-named `this`-method exists but NONE targets the receiver's TEMPLATE base (via new sema_struct_template_name — compares template-to-template, not the mangled specialized name), emit `no method `<m>` on `<Receiver(Args)>``; a case-insensitive prefix/suffix near-miss on the same receiver adds `; did you mean `<x>`?` (`at`->`copyAt`). Gated so compiler intrinsics with no user decl (toString/toJson/fromJson/Task.get) still reach the backend. Added sema_receiver_display (renders `List(Int)` from the template base + resolved generic args) and sema_name_near. Verified: `xs.at(index:0)` -> "no method `at` on `List(Int)`; did you mean `copyAt`?" at the .rae site; String.at/toString/toJson/valid copyAt unaffected; no `add` false positives. Also gated on a CONCRETELY-typed receiver: a chained call sema leaves unresolved types its result Void (`text.at(index:i).toInt()`), and erroring there false-flags valid backend-resolved calls — skip Void/Unknown/Any receivers. Test 672_no_method_on_receiver_diag.

Compile-time, zero runtime cost, no new primitive. Acceptance: mutating the aliased List inside a live `modAt`/`viewAt` `if let` body is a sema error; mutating a DIFFERENT List and `copyAt`+`if let` still compile; test added; suite green. Deps: none; blocks the `view`/`mod` half of #650 for any site whose body mutates the container. DONE 2026-08-27 — Option A implemented (sema.c AST_STMT_IF, inside the if-let binding block). When the binding source is `list.viewAt/modAt(index:)` (method-call form) or `viewAt/modAt(list, index:)` (plain-call form), the aliased List is the receiver/first-arg; each then-branch statement is run through the EXISTING `sema_stmt_mutates_collection` (reused verbatim, so it catches nested blocks too), and any of the structural mutators (add/set/insert/remove/swapRemove/clear/drop/grow/pop) on that same List is a sema error: "cannot mutate a List while a `viewAt`/`modAt` binding aliases one of its elements" (the loop diagnostic reworded). `copyAt` (a detached value binding, uses `=` not `=>`) and mutating a DIFFERENT List stay legal; verified both plus a no-mutation viewAt body. Compile-time, zero runtime cost, no new primitive. Test 673_viewat_modat_aliasing_borrow.
- [x] #659 Require `copy` for cascade-drop value bindings (from #646; design note: docs/copy-mode-cascade-drop.md). DECISION POINT: adopt the requirement, OR keep status quo and pursue move-on-last-use instead — see the note's "honest caveat" (the benefit is explicitness/auditability, NOT perf or correctness; today's implicit bind already deep-copies safely). If adopting: make a bare value binding `let x: T = y` a sema error when `type_needs_cascade_drop(T)` is true, with message naming the fix (write `copy T` to deep-copy, or `view`/`mod` to alias); `copy T` binding deep-copies (the existing `rae_deep_copy_<T>` codegen — no new codegen needed); non-cascade-drop types (Int/Vec2/Particle) keep the implicit plain copy. Migrate existing `let x: HeapOwningStruct = y` callers to `copy` (or a `view`/`mod` alias). Acceptance: owning struct bound by value WITHOUT `copy` errors; WITH `copy` deep-copies with no double free (RAE_MEM_STATS outstanding=0); `Particle`/`Point`/`Vec2` still bind without `copy`; suite green. Note: `is_copy` is currently annotation-only for LOCAL bindings (only parameter passing honors it), so the change is primarily the sema gate + routing the local `copy` binding through the existing deep-copy path. Deps: relates to #641 (drop/deep-copy helper generation). QUESTION 2026-08-27: This is a language-semantics change flagged as a DECISION POINT, and measurement shows adopting it as literally specified is not viable. I prototyped the exact gate (bare value binding of a `type_needs_cascade_drop` type from a place expr -> error) and ran the full suite: 275 of 333 cases FAIL to compile. Root cause: `String` is cascade-drop, so `let name: String = <place>` is flagged — one of the most common patterns in the language — and it pervades lib/ (string.rae, filesystem.rae, app3d/*, ui/*), so nearly every test aborts at a lib-level String binding before reaching its own code. The note's examples/acceptance only ever cite STRUCTS (Owner/Particle/Point/Vec2) and never bare String, so whether bare String is in scope is a genuine ambiguity that dominates the cost. Per the note's own honest caveat the benefit is ONLY explicitness/auditability — NOT perf (copy deep-copies identically to today's implicit bind) and NOT correctness (already safe, outstanding=0). Which do you want? (A) Adopt as specified incl. String — ~hundreds of `copy String` migrations across lib/tests/examples, high friction; (B) Adopt but EXCLUDE bare String / primitive-ish heap types, gating ONLY user structs/containers that own heap (few sites: SdfFont/List/Holder + a handful) — a usable middle that keeps the auditability win for the aggregates the note actually cites; (C) Keep status quo (implicit deep copy is safe) and instead pursue move-on-last-use (the note's finding #1) as the higher-value follow-up. RECOMMENDATION: (B) if we want the explicitness win now (smallest churn, matches the note's struct-focused examples), else (C). Gate prototype reverted; no code committed. DECISION 2026-08-27 (user): option (C) — KEEP STATUS QUO. Bare value bindings deep-copy implicitly for every type, as today. Reason: options (A) and (B) both make the need for `copy` depend on what a type CONTAINS, so changing `Int` into a heap-owning type would change which code compiles — Rae's rule is that every type follows the same rules. The 275 failures from `String` being cascade-drop are that hazard demonstrated, not a reason to exempt `String`. No compiler change. Higher-value follow-up (move-on-last-use, optimization-only, no type-dependent rule) filed to QUEUE_BACKLOG.md as #662.

DONE 2026-09-01 — New lib/ecs/event.rae with EventQueue(T) { events: List(T), reserve: List(T) } — the double-buffered per-frame event channel, evolved from Queue(T)'s design. eventSend appends to `events` (one system PRODUCES), eventCount/eventAt drain it in order (later systems CONSUME the SAME frame), eventFrameAdvance (once per frame after all consumers) recycles via the double buffer: clear the spare then SWAP it in as the fresh events buffer (`var tmp = own this.events; this.events = own this.reserve; this.reserve = own tmp` — the owned-List move-swap compiles) so next frame starts empty with no per-event teardown and consumer indices stay valid all frame. DONE: both layout phases now walk the cached parent-before-child `depthOrder` (#713) linearly instead of recursing — the same pattern #727 used for transforms. Measure (bottom-up) walks the order in REVERSE: `measureLinear` calls `measureNode` on each entity, so every child's MeasuredSize is written before its parent reads it (reverse pre-order ⇒ all descendants precede their ancestor). Compute (top-down) walks it FORWARD: `computeLinear` seeds each root's ComputedRect (`seedRoot`) then `placeChildren` places active kids; the place{Horizontal,Vertical,Stack} helpers now `writeComputedRect` each child directly (position + own Offset, resolved size) instead of recursing — the loop reaches each child later and reads its ComputedRect.size as ownW/ownH. Standalone roots (no Parent, no Children) are absent from the order so both phases sweep `alive` for them. No true recursion remains in layout. File hit the compiler's HARD 1000-line cap, so the compute/placement half was split into a new sibling module `lib/ui/LayoutSystem/LayoutPlace.rae` (563 + 507 LOC), imported by LayoutSystem.rae so it rides into every consumer's build graph. DoD: the let-then-view idiom no longer double-frees.  [LANG-CHECK: after finishing, note in docs/ecs-language-wishlist.md any missing Rae language feature that would have made this task easier or cleaner — add a bullet only if it is new there; skip if nothing new.] DONE: root cause was NOT the drop path (sema.c/c_backend.c) but the runtime producer rae_json_build (the toJson result builder): unlike every other owned-String producer (rae_ext_rae_str_interp/concat etc.), it neither mem-tagged NOR pool-registered its malloc. The C backend emits owned method results as pool temps — pool_take hands ownership to a local, a surrounding pool_flush frees an inlined temp — so an unregistered toJson result bound to a local (`let s = obj.toJson()`) was freed as an UNTRACKED heap (one 'unknown free' per call -> RAE_MEM_STATS TOTAL outstanding=-1), while the INLINED form silently LEAKED it (untagged, invisible). Fix: moved rae_json_build from a header static-inline to runtime_buffers_math.c (next to rae_json_extract_string, where rae_mem_str_tag is visible) and made it mem-tag + pool-register its result. Now both the let-then-view idiom AND the inlined form are clean. Note: _outstanding() deliberately skips the UNKNOWN site, so this class of over-free was invisible to it — added rae_ext_rae_mem_stats_unknown_frees() and test 712_tojson_let_view_no_double_free (5000 iters: 5000 untracked frees WITHOUT the fix -> verdict OVERFREE, 0 WITH -> OK; toggled the fix off/on to prove the guard bites). Full suite green (372 cases + 66 examples); existing json/serialize tests (691/696/698/700/703/710) unaffected. LANG-CHECK: nothing new — a runtime producer-protocol consistency fix, not an ECS language-feature gap.

Release vs destroy vs copy: only wgpu*Release, never Destroy; ID copy has no native effect. Abandoned recordings: dropping an unsubmitted Recording releases its encoder (no manager access needed, so nothing leaks); submit takes mod Recording and SPENDS it (own params are read-only in Rae). shutdown polls once without waiting, treats the rest as finished so deferred releases proceed, then the destructor releases dependents-first; also the device-loss path. - [x] #1002 {difficulty:5} Realistic water glitches or has maybe a deltatime error when the camera moves. The waves are ok when not moving hte camera, but when it moves, there is extra speed or something glitchy in the waves. Fix. THis had an earlier attempt at a fix, but after testing, it is still broken. Not fixed. Especially when I press shift key, when moving the camera, it seems that time flows at extra speed. DONE (second attempt; the first one — moving waterDraw's time accumulation past its early returns — was a no-op for 119, whose wave time is absolute wall clock). Root cause is SPATIAL, not deltaTime: in 119_ocean_fft the three FFT cascade maps (250/60/8 m tiles, 256 texels, NO mips) were summed unfaded (a) per VERTEX on the camera-centred radial grid, whose cells grow to metres/tens of metres with distance, and (b) per PIXEL for normals + Jacobian foam. Short cascades sampled on coarse cells alias into wide bands that re-shuffle every metre the mesh snaps to the camera, and far pixels are point samples of unrelated waves — so the far sea flickers/'speeds up' exactly in proportion to camera speed (shift = 4x). Fix in lib/water: waterSurface.wgsl fades each cascade out of the vertex displacement where its longest wave spans under ~4-8 grid cells (cascadeVertexWeight, the FFT twin of waveGridFactor) and out of the slope/foam where the pixel footprint (dpdx/dpdy of the world xy) exceeds ~1.5-4 texels of that cascade (cascadePixelWeight). New `grid` vec4 in the Water uniform (80 floats): WaterBody.clipCellPerMetre / clipFirstCell (ClipMap.radialGridCellPerMetre(segments, growth); 119 sets them from its 96 / 1.09 grid), fftSize and cascadeBandBins (moved to Water.rae, shared with WaterFft). Verified: frozen test frame at camera x = 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 (new RAE_WATER_CAMERA_X knob) — mean pixel diff of the far bands for a 0.5 m step fell 7.1->0.7, 20.5->11.2, 21.2->15.0 while the near bands (real parallax) are unchanged; the horizon reads as a coherent swell instead of white speckle; gates 119 (screenshot + 14 tier stages) and 114 (shared shader, toon lake) PASS.

[LANG-CHECK: after finishing, note in docs/ecs-language-wishlist.md any missing Rae language feature that would have made this task easier or cleaner — add a bullet only if it is new there; skip if nothing new.] DONE — CLOSED AS NOT-NEEDED (the DoD's second branch), reasoning recorded in docs/compile-time-reflection.md (new "Construction via `fields(Type)` — decided NOT to build (#774)" section + Status line + open-questions bullet marked RESOLVED). The built-in gate ("only start if #760/#768/#771 show a real need") is NOT met, and the assessment against the current tree is decisive: (1) The failure mode reflection would prevent is ALREADY a compile error — Rae builds a struct from a literal with EVERY field present, so createUiWorld/createWorld3d/createGameWorld cannot silently drop a table the way a hand-listed clear/serialize loop can (that silent-drop risk is exactly why the CLEAR + SERIALIZE halves DID land via fields(value) in #760/#772/#773). Reflection buys no safety here, only brevity. (2) It is the cheapest boilerplate, written once per world, one line per field. (3) It is the MOST expensive to implement for the least gain: unlike clear/serialize which ITERATE an existing value, construction has no value to iterate and no incremental-assembly form in the language (a struct is built all-at-once from a literal) — a generic createWorld(W: type) would need type-level fields(Type), a NEW struct-assembly construct (the unsolved "how the loop assembles the literal" open question), AND per-field-kind match dispatch because the worlds are NON-uniform (alongside ComponentTable(T) they carry EntityAllocator, a StringMap `UiWorld.nodeIds`, a `GameWorld.hierarchyOrder`, and a scalar `GameWorld.splashTick: 0`); that match+assembly is plausibly as much code as the three explicit constructors plus large new compiler machinery. (4) No real need surfaced — #771/#793-797 added World3d and used the explicit createWorld3d (6 tables) without friction. LANG-CHECK: nothing NEW — the enabling gap (no incremental struct assembly) is already covered by the wishlist's "Synthesize a world from its component set" bullet (whose design doc IS compile-time-reflection.md); I did NOT add a duplicate bullet, only kept that existing bullet's status accurate (noting the construction half was declined). - [x] #798 {difficulty:4} [compiler] Fix move-vs-copy for a named heap-owning local placed into a struct-literal FIELD. Found in #795: `var world: World3d = createWorld3d(); ...; ret TetrisRenderState { world: world, ... }` shallow-COPIES `world` instead of moving it, so the local and the struct field share the same ComponentTable buffers and BOTH drop them at scope exit -> double-free (SIGTRAP in libsystem_malloc free, via rae_drop_struct_rae_World3d -> ComponentTable drop -> rae_buf_free). `ret namedLocal` (whole return value) DOES move correctly (buildScene #794, buildTetrisWorld), and an INLINE rvalue in a struct field moves too (World3dAsset `{ world: buildWorld3dFromScene3d(...) }`) — only a NAMED local as the last use in a struct-literal field is mishandled. Workaround shipped in 97: build via a helper returning World3d and inline it in the literal. Fix: treat a named local's last use inside a struct-literal field as a MOVE (or, if a copy is intended, deep-copy the heap). Verify: a repro (own-heap local -> struct field, no use after) drops exactly once; full suite green. DoD: the pattern moves rather than double-frees, and 97's helper workaround can be simplified back if desired. DONE. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via minimal repro): `ret Struct { field: namedLocal }` where the field type transitively owns a NON-deep-copyable type (a `ComponentTable` inside `World3d`) took the struct-field deep-copy path (c_expr.c) — but the SYNTHESISED `rae_deep_copy_<T>` shallow-copies such a field (`dst->table = src->table`) instead of erroring like a DIRECT ComponentTable field does; the local is then dropped at scope exit → the field and the local free the same buffers twice (SIGABRT in rae_ext_rae_buf_free). FIX (the task's preferred MOVE): a bare owning LOCAL used as a struct-literal field is now MOVED when that literal IS the function's return value (last use is guaranteed). New `CFuncContext.return_value_expr` (set to the ret value node around its emit in c_stmt.c) lets the struct-field emitter (c_expr.c) recognise the exact `ret Struct { f: local }` node; for a bare owning (non view/mod) LET/var local appearing exactly once in that literal it emits the bare value (ownership transfer) and marks the local moved (mark_local_moved_by_name) so the return epilogue's implicit-drop pass skips it — no deep-copy, no double-free. Tightly scoped: only the exact return-value literal (nested/wrapped literals and non-return `let x = Struct{ f: local }` still deep-copy, verified a local USED AFTER still deep-copies correctly); owned-String fields keep their existing path; parameters keep their own move logic. VERIFIED: new case 731_ret_struct_field_move (World-wrapping-ComponentTable moved through a struct field, drops exactly once — SIGABRT'd before the fix, clean after); emitted C for the repro + 97 shows `.field = local` (bare move) not a deep-copy. SIMPLIFIED 97 back: inlined buildTetrisWorld into createTetrisRenderState using the now-safe `ret TetrisRenderState { world: world, ... }` named-local pattern (helper removed); 97 renders non-blank (829 colours). Full suite green via watch-tests.sh (RAE_RUN_END exit=0): cases 391 pass/0 fail (incl. 731), examples 66 pass/0 fail; the ownership/leak regression tests (432_mobile_ui_leak_regression, 425-453 owning-field/move suite) all pass — no double-free or leak regressions from the codegen change.

STATE: multi-type-param generic inference LANDED (#707), but joins are hand-written PER ARITY — only `query2`/`query3` exist (lib/ecs/Query.rae), no `query4`+, and consuming a result is still the verbose index+accessor form (`componentCount` + `componentEntityAt(i)` + `componentDataAt(i)` + `componentGet`). NOT variadic / type-list generics — that is metaprogramming and is DECLINED. (2) ITERATION SUGAR — `for (entity, mod a, mod b) in query(world, A, B)` desugaring to the join walk with mod/view binding modes preserved; this is the real boilerplate win on the single most-used ECS operation. (3) FILTERS as PLAIN FUNCTIONS, not a builder: `with T`/`without T` is just "is the tag/component present on this entity" (an O(1) sparse check), and change-detection ("only entities whose A changed since last run") is a plain comparison against the `generation`/`denseStamps` the tables ALREADY carry. NO composable query-builder object / mini-DSL — DECLINED as a framework creeping in. Keep every join O(smallest table): drive off the smallest ComponentTable, O(1) sparse membership on the rest — exactly how query2/query3 work. This is the data-oriented core, what a performance engineer hand-writes; the task only removes the boilerplate around it. DoD: a short design note in the wishlist with the maintainer's sign-off on the sugar spelling; then query4/query5 + the iteration sugar + with/without + change-detection as plain functions, with tests (4-/5-way join, tag filter, change-detection skip, mod write-through). Refs: #707, docs/ecs-api-reference.md. PROGRESS — the NON-SYNTAX half is DONE, verified and committed; the iteration SUGAR needs your sign-off on its spelling before it can be built (it is new syntax, and AGENTS.md forbids adding syntax without approval). LANDED in lib/ecs/Query.rae: (1) `query4`/`query5` + `Query4Match`/`Query5Match` + `query4ViewA..D`/`query5ViewA..E`, hand-written in exactly the query2/query3 smallest-table-probe style (iterate the smallest table, O(1) sparse probe on the rest, O(min table)) — a FIXED ladder, no variadic generics; (2) filters as plain functions, no builder: `with T` is the existing `tagged(data, tag)`; NEW `without(data, tag)` (entities lacking the tag — a negation walks the data table, one O(1) probe each); NEW `changedSince(table, sinceGeneration)` (per-ENTITY change-detection read straight off the `denseStamps` the table already keeps — a system records `componentTableGeneration` after a run and passes it next time; complements Schedule's table-level skip). TESTS: 732_ecs_query4_query5 (4-/5-way joins with the smallest table landing in different driver slots, view reads, mod write-through read-back) and 733_ecs_query_filters (with/without/changedSince incl. the idle skip case). Full suite GREEN via watch-tests.sh (RAE_RUN_END exit=0: cases 393/0, examples 66/0). DOCS: docs/ecs-api-reference.md query section extended (query4/5, the three filters) and three drift bugs fixed (`hit.denseA`->`indexA`, `queryTagged`->`tagged`, `query.rae`->`Query.rae`); the sugar design note is written into docs/ecs-language-wishlist.md "Ergonomic query iteration". FINDING that shapes the question: the verbose index+accessor form the wishlist complained about is ALREADY gone — a query returns match records with each entity's dense index, so today's idiom is one line per component (`let p: mod Pos => queryModAt(table: pos, denseIndex: hit.indexA)`). The only sugar left is binding components in the loop head; Rae has no `for` and no tuple destructuring, so the informal `for (entity, mod a, mod b) in query(...)` sketch is not Rae — the one spelling that fits the grammar is a MULTI-BINDING loop head with POSITIONAL binding->table mapping: `loop let entity: EntityId, p: mod Pos, v: view Vel in query2(tableA: pos, tableB: vel) { … }` (desugars to the match loop + accessor aliases; a `mod` binding bumps the stamp like queryModAt, a `view` binding does not). Honest lens: not a second vocabulary and it is on the hottest path, but the payoff is ONE saved line per component, it adds an implicit positional mapping, and it costs parser+sema+codegen — a performance engineer does not need it. QUESTION: for the iteration sugar, pick one — (A) ADOPT the multi-binding `loop let entity: EntityId, p: mod Pos, v: view Vel in query2(...)` as the single blessed spelling and I implement it (parser+sema+codegen, positional binding->table, mod/view modes preserved, tests), or (B) DECLINE the sugar and keep the explicit one-line-per-component accessor form as the idiom (consistent with the data-oriented lens; I would then record it in the wishlist as a decision and close this task). My lean is (B). Which? DONE (option A chosen by the maintainer). The ECS QUERY LOOP is now a first-class statement: `loop let entity: EntityId, p: mod Pos, v: view Vel in query2(tableA: pos, tableB: vel) { p.x = p.x + v.v }` — works over query2..query5 and forEach (bare or `Query.`-qualified); an optional leading `EntityId` binding receives the entity; the remaining bindings map POSITIONALLY to the joined tables and must be `mod` (writes through, bumps the change stamp exactly like queryModAt) or `view` (never dirties); nested query loops each own their own result. IMPLEMENTATION: pure sugar resolved in the PARSER (compiler/src/parser.c parse_query_loop) — the statement expands to a two-statement chain: a hoisted hidden owned `let raeQueryHits<N>: List(QueryNMatch) = query…(…)` plus the match loop `loop let raeQueryHit<N>: view QueryNMatch in raeQueryHits<N>` whose body is prefixed with `let entity = hit.entity` and one `let p: mod T => queryModAt(table: pos, denseIndex: hit.indexA)` / `queryViewAt` alias per component. Sema and codegen are UNTOUCHED and see ordinary Rae, so the compiled C is byte-for-byte the hand-written idiom. The hoist matters: codegen snapshots a loop iterable once but explicitly does not own/drop it, so iterating a call directly would have leaked the result list every loop — hoisting into an owned `let` makes ownership identical to the hand-written form. parse_block now walks a returned statement chain when appending (a no-op for every other statement) and parallelLoop marks the loop inside the chain. DIAGNOSTICS (parse-time, exact caret): component-count vs table-count mismatch; a component binding that is neither mod nor view; a non-query iterable; a computed table argument (must be a name/field path because the component is aliased back into that same table). TESTS: 734_ecs_query_loop (query2 entity+mod+view with read-back, view-only loop leaves the table generation unchanged, query3 with two mod bindings, forEach single-table, nested query loops) + rejects 735_reject_query_loop_arity and 736_reject_query_loop_mode (expected.txt captured from the real diagnostics). DOCS: docs/ecs-api-reference.md "The query loop — Rae's native join walk" (rules + the exact desugaring) and docs/ecs-language-wishlist.md marks the iteration-sugar item DECIDED (A) + LANDED with the rationale: a language that bets on ECS should make its most common operation its cleanest line, and it costs nothing at runtime. Together with the earlier half (query4/query5 fixed ladder, without, changedSince as plain functions) this closes #807. [>claude]->[x].

- [x] #810 {difficulty:2} [stdlib+docs] Stable dense-iteration order — DOCUMENT the guarantee (the default); do NOT add an ordered structure unless a named system provably needs it. Migrations rely on "dense order == insertion order" for render-submit order and pool slots, but `componentRemove` does a swap-remove that silently REORDERS the table — an undocumented invariant that can break a render pass or pool with no compile error. The swap-remove is the CORRECT data-oriented choice (O(1) remove, keeps the array dense); order instability is its honest cost, so the fix is to write the truth down, not to compromise the layout. DO: (a) document the exact guarantee in docs/ecs-api-reference.md ("dense order is insertion order UNTIL the first swap-remove, then unspecified") and AUDIT every order-dependent system (render submit, pool slots) so each either provably holds under that rule or is made order-independent (e.g. sort by a stable key at submit). ONLY IF a specific system is found that genuinely cannot be made order-independent, then (b) add the SMALLEST explicit opt-in — e.g. an order-preserving `componentRemove` variant at O(n) used by THAT table alone — never a general ordered index paying memory on every table. Cheap correctness win. DoD: guarantee written; audit recorded per system; a test pins the chosen behaviour across a remove. DONE — option (a) throughout; NO ordered structure was added. CONTRACT written in docs/ecs-api-reference.md as a dedicated "Iteration-order contract (#810)" section: dense order is insertion order UNTIL the first non-tail componentRemove; a non-tail remove is a swap-remove that moves the LAST row into the hole (its data and change stamp move with it, sparse map repointed, array stays dense — the deliberate O(1) data-oriented choice); after that, order is UNSPECIFIED; removing the TAIL leaves the rest untouched; dense indices / QueryNMatch are valid only for the current walk, never across a structural mutation or frames; never derive draw order, pool slots or "the first one" from dense order — carry the key as a component field or pick by a stable key. Also records WHY there is deliberately no order-preserving remove and no ordered index (memory/O(n) on every table for a convenience no system needs), and the smallest opt-in if a future system ever genuinely needs it. FIX: report the statement's OWN file — decls already carry `origin_file` (stamped at merge); thread the enclosing decl's origin_file (or a per-statement file) into sema_analyze_stmt/sema_analyze_expr and use it in diag_error instead of module->file_path, falling back to module->file_path when unknown. Sema diagnostics now name the file the offending code actually lives in. FINDING: the infrastructure already existed — sema keeps a static `s_current_decl_origin` (the decl being analysed) that import/alias resolution already keys on, and a handful of diagnostics already preferred it — but 28 `diag_error(module->file_path, …)` sites (incl. the #658 List rule and the #814 table rule), 4 `const char* file = module->file_path` lookups and a `diag_report` bypassed it, and the origin was only set around FUNCTION BODIES, so a global-let initializer or type-level error had no origin at all. FIX (compiler/src/sema.c): one helper `sema_diag_file(module)` = `s_current_decl_origin ? … : module->file_path`; every diagnostic site routed through it mechanically (28 diag_error + 9 explicit ternaries normalised + 4 file lookups + 1 diag_report — `diag_error(module->file_path` no longer occurs); and `sema_analyze_decl` is wrapped so the origin is saved/set/restored around EVERY decl kind, not just function bodies. Scope semantics untouched (resolution already used the origin); fallback to the merged path only when no decl is current (specialization/backend entry points). (b) C emitter: an integer literal above INT64_MAX, or ANY integer literal in a UInt64-typed context, is emitted `((uint64_t)…ULL)`; the binary-op expected-type picker no longer demotes a UInt64 expectation to the literal's plain `Int` (so a local `let y: UInt64 = 4294967295 * 4294967295` multiplies in uint64). In lib/water/waterFft.wgsl (composed like GrassCompute): a compute pass that fills a per-cascade h0 spectrum texture from a TMA/JONSWAP-style spectrum with directional (Hasselmann) spreading (wind speed/direction, fetch, cascade tile size -> k grid), run ONCE per resolution/params change, plus the Stockham butterfly texture (twiddles + read indices per stage, no bit-reversal) once per FFT size. Verify by a low-res READBACK (the grass diagnostics path): h0 is non-zero, Hermitian-symmetric, and its energy peaks at the JONSWAP peak frequency. Technique only from GodotOceanWaves / inkwell-webgpu-water — do NOT copy code (no license). DONE. lib/water/waterFft.wgsl (from the Tessendorf / Hasselmann / Bouws papers — no code copied): `spectrum` fills a cascade's h0 rgba32float storage texture: k = 2pi/L (x - N/2, y - N/2); JONSWAP S(w) (fetch-limited: w_p = 22 (g^2/(U F))^(1/3), alpha = 0.076 (U^2/(F g))^0.22, gamma 3.3, sigma 0.07/0.09) x the TMA finite-depth factor x Hasselmann 1980 spreading D = N(s) cos^(2s)(theta/2) with s(w/w_p) and the normalisation 2^(2s-1)/pi * G(s+1)^2 / G(2s+1) via a Stirling ln-Gamma; times the Jacobian (dw/dk)/k with w^2 = g k tanh(kh); amplitude sqrt(2E) dk; complex Gaussian from a PCG hash + Box-Muller seeded per (cascade, texel) so a texel is deterministic; k = 0 and the Nyquist row/column zeroed (their -k is themselves); packed (h0(k), h0(-k)) per texel. `butterfly` fills the per-output radix-2 Stockham table (log2N columns x N rows): stage s, span Ns: block = i/2Ns, k = i mod 2Ns, reads j = block*Ns + (k mod Ns) and j + N/2, twiddle exp(+2pi i (k mod Ns)/2Ns) with the sign folded for k >= Ns — inverse, autosort, no bit reversal. WaterSystem: ensureFftGpu builds two compute pipelines from the one module (each entry point gets its OWN pipeline + bind group — wgpu derives a layout from the bindings an entry point uses), a 3-vec4 FftU uniform, the butterfly texture, per-cascade h0 textures, a MapRead staging buffer; bakeFftSpectrum runs ONCE per params (waterFftInvalidate re-bakes), one uniform upload + one submitted dispatch per cascade, then the butterfly. Cascade bands: kLow/kHigh per cascade so the summed cascades never count a wavelength twice; hand-over at kHigh = cascadeBandBins(6) * 2pi/L_next — the readback showed the naive 2pi/L_next boundary gave the 250 m cascade a 4-cell (56-texel) disc of its 256x256 grid. WaterBody carries the sea state: windSpeed 9, windDirRad 0.7, fetch 250 km, waterDepth 50 (=> k_p 0.0603 rad/m, a 104 m peak wavelength). VERIFICATION by READBACK (the grass map-read idiom; blocking, diagnostics only): readbackFloat4 copies an rgba32float texture to the staging buffer with bytesPerRow padded to the 256-byte COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW_ALIGNMENT (the 8-wide butterfly needs it — the first run panicked exactly there) and maps it into a List(Float); waterFftDiagnose checks (a) non-zero texels match the band's k-space disc pi (kHigh/dk)^2 within 0.6..1.3x, (b) EXACT (k,-k) packing symmetry — texel(k).zw == texel(-k).xy, measured 0, (c) the radial energy peak bin vs the JONSWAP k_p bin — measured peak bin 2 vs expected 2.40 (within 2), (d) butterfly stage 0 reads (i/2, i/2 + N/2) with twiddle +-1 — true. 118 runs the diagnose under RAE_WATER_FFT_DIAG=1 at its second water frame and its gate now asserts "[water fft] h0 ok"; PASS. Compute passes: evolve h0 -> h(k,t) (dispersion w = sqrt(g k), plus the x/y choppiness and slope terms packed as extra complex channels), then the Stockham iFFT: row pass over the stages reading the butterfly texture, transpose, reuse the same row pass for columns; write displacement (x,y,z), normal and the Jacobian/foam map into the #831 cascade textures (rgba16float storage). VERIFY THE FFT HONESTLY: seed a KNOWN single-frequency spectrum, run the iFFT, read back one row and assert the expected sine (amplitude + period) — the only real correctness check; then the JONSWAP field for non-NaN, bounded displacement. Needs on-hardware iteration. DONE. lib/water/waterFft.wgsl gained the per-frame path: `evolve` — h(k,t) = h0(k) e^(iwt) + conj(h0(-k)) e^(-iwt) with w^2 = g k tanh(kh), then the field pair this dispatch packs as Z = A + iB: (h, Dx), (Dy, dh/dx), (dh/dy, dDx/dx), (dDy/dy, dDx/dy) with Dx = -i (kx/k) h etc. — TWO real fields per complex transform, valid because every field's spectrum is Hermitian (h(-k) = conj h(k)), so the inverse transform's real part is A and its imaginary part B; `stockham` — one radix-2 stage along x for every row, reading (twiddle, a, b) from the #849 butterfly column `stage`; `transpose`; the same stage shader for the columns; `fieldOut` un-transposes into the per-field result; `post` — undo the centred spectrum's (-1)^(x+y), chop by WaterBody.choppiness (new field, 1.2), normal from the slopes, Jacobian J = (1 + l dDx/dx)(1 + l dDy/dy) - l^2 dDx/dy^2, foam = clamp(1 - J) — into the #831 cascade maps (rgba16float storage). WaterFft.waterFftUpdate encodes ALL of it as ONE compute pass in ONE submit (dispatches in a pass see earlier storage writes): per cascade x field: evolve -> P, log2N stages ping-ponging P/Q, transpose, log2N stages, fieldOut -> R_f; then post; ~230 dispatches/frame for 3 x 256^2. Sources are bound as texture_2d<f32> (core textureLoad), only destinations as storage textures (no non-core storage reads); per-(cascade, field) evolve uniforms and per-stage uniforms because a single submit forbids rewriting one buffer between dispatches. Runs every frame only for body.style = realistic (toon bodies never read the maps). ARCHITECTURE: WaterSystem.rae crossed the 1000-line hard cap (the compiler enforces it) — the whole FFT (cascades, bake, frame, diagnostics, releases, waterShutdown) moved to lib/water/WaterFft.rae (765 lines; WaterSystem.rae 331); callers open water/WaterFft. C handle store widened to 160 slots. THE HONEST FFT TEST (waterFftDiagnoseIfft, run by 118 under RAE_WATER_FFT_DIAG=1 and asserted by its gate as "[water fft] ifft ok"): `spectrum` has a test mode that seeds ONE known wave (h0 = 0.25 at k index +-(3, 0), so h = 0.5 at both at t = 0) whose unnormalised inverse transform must be exactly cos(2pi 3x/N) of amplitude 1 — read back row N/2 of the height field, sign-corrected by (-1)^(x+y): MEASURED amplitude 1 (expect 1), value at x = 0 = 1 (expect 1), zero crossings 6 (expect 6), finite; then JONSWAP re-baked and transformed at t = 1: finite, height max 0.084 m (a 9 m/s sea on the 250 m tile). - [x] #884 {difficulty:4} [compiler/ownership] A produced value passed straight to a `view`/`mod` parameter is never released — legal code that silently leaks. VERIFIED example (compiles and runs): given `func create(id: view Int) ret Slot`, `func drop(this: mod Slot)`, and `func inspect(slot: view Slot) ret Int { ret slot.id }`, the line `let seen: Int = inspect(slot: create(id: 1))` logs `acquire 1` then `seen 1` but NEVER `release 1`, while `let kept: Slot = create(id: 2)` followed by `inspect(slot: kept)` DOES log `release 2` at scope exit. Reproduce: two sibling `if let ... { var a: Recording = ...; a.drop() }` / `if let ... { var doomed: Recording = ...; (no drop) }` blocks in one function with `func drop(this: mod Recording)` — the second block's scope-exit drop is emitted as a flag-guarded drop without the flag declaration. Found while writing 795_gpu_lifetime_model (#870), which now abandons by scope exit instead. Fix: scope the explicit-drop live flag to the exact local (declare it where that local is declared) instead of keying on the type/name across sibling scopes; add a regression. Deps: none. DONE. Root cause: the runtime live-flag `int __rae_live_<name>` (c_stmt.c, #885) is tracked per LOCAL SLOT INDEX in CFuncContext.local_drop_flag[], and a slot index is REUSED across sibling scopes within one function — an if-let/loop/match-case body's locals pop back to `saved_locals` on scope exit, so the next sibling scope's first local claims the SAME index. Three of the seven let-declaration sites in emit_stmt_inner already reset local_drop_flag[idx]=false when a new local claims a slot (if-let binding, opt-box payload unwrap, collection-loop element); the other four (the general let/var path, a materialised-bind ref, a mod-alias-to-array-element ref, and a collection-literal-initialized local) did not — so a local explicitly `.drop()`-ed in one sibling scope (flag declared + set true) left that stale `true` for whatever unrelated local next occupied the slot; the scope-exit drop pass then emitted `if (__rae_live_<newName>) {...}` guarding the NEW local's name, but that flag was never declared for it (gcc: use of undeclared identifier). Fixed by adding the same `local_drop_flag[idx] = false` reset at all four missing sites, matching the existing pattern — the flag is now always scoped to the exact local it is declared for, never leaked from whatever local last occupied the slot. Audited match-statement case bodies too (case pattern list.c: 2647): they save/restore local_count exactly like if-let and route through the SAME emit_stmt LET paths, so no separate fix was needed there — verified directly with a match-case sibling repro. Verified: reproduced the task's exact repro (sibling if-let with `var a: Recording ... a.drop()` then `var doomed: Recording` with no drop) and its exact gcc error before the fix; after, both drop exactly once. Also verified four alternating explicit/implicit sibling if-let blocks and a match-case sibling variant, all correct. New regression compiler/tests/cases/808_sibling_if_let_explicit_drop_flag (four alternating sibling if-lets); bisected against the pre-fix compiler via git stash — it reproduces the identical undeclared-identifier error (7 errors, flags leaking through TWO further sibling blocks) and passes after the fix. NO VISUAL TESTS run. Full non-visual watch-tests unit suite: 468 passed, 0 failed, exit 0 (467 prior + the new 808 case).

- [x] #926 {difficulty:4} [compiler] Sema does not check call ARGUMENTS against the callee's parameters — clang does, late and badly. Three shapes, all reproduced on eef257be with a two-parameter `func takesTwo(alpha: view Int, beta: view Int)`: (a) a MISSING argument `takesTwo(alpha: 1)` and (b) an EXTRA one `takesTwo(alpha: 1, beta: 2, gamma: 3)` pass sema and die in the emitted C as `call to undeclared function 'rae_takesTwo'` (the mangled name embeds the arity, so the C symbol does not exist); (c) worst, a WRONG NAME `takesTwo(alpha: 1, gamma: 2)` compiles, runs and prints 3 — the argument is bound positionally and the name is never compared, which defeats the whole named-argument design (the name at the call site is supposed to be checked information, not decoration). Found migrating a downstream game across #869/#873/#907–#915: every call whose signature had gained a `resources:`/`canvas:` parameter sailed through sema and surfaced only as fourteen clang errors naming `rae_grassGenerate`, `rae_beginPass`, `rae_renderSystemGpu2d`, … Fix: resolve the call against the parameter list in sema — unknown name, missing non-defaulted parameter, duplicate, and extra argument are each a diagnostic at the call site naming the callee and its signature (like #751's unknown-function message). Add negative fixtures for all three shapes plus a positive one for defaulted parameters (#14) so the fix cannot regress them. DONE. Sema now resolves every bare and module-qualified call against the callee's parameter list (compiler/src/sema.c, #926 helpers): (a) missing / (b) extra argument -> `call to 'takesTwo' has 1 argument but it takes 2: takesTwo(alpha: view Int, beta: view Int)` (all signatures listed for an arity-overloaded name; skipped when an open GENERIC candidate exists, since a positional type argument legitimately changes the count and such calls are bound by name in the backend); (c) wrong name -> `argument 'gamma' does not match parameter 'beta' of takesTwo(...)` (arguments stay positional; the name is checked at its position, a bare type argument to a generic is skipped); plus duplicate names -> `duplicate argument 'alpha' in call to ...`. Fixtures 831 (missing), 832 (extra), 833 (wrong name), 834 (duplicate) and positive 835 (positional first arg, all-named, arity overload, generic with type arg, module-qualified). NOTE: Rae has NO defaulted parameters (AstParam has no default; #14 in the task text refers to a defer/terrain commit, not defaults), so a 'defaulted parameter' positive fixture cannot exist — 835 says so; 'missing non-defaulted' == missing. The new check found 24 latent mismatches in the tree, all fixed: 2 REAL mass-rename bugs (94 beginFrame `game: 0.05` for `g:`, 97 Hud drawRoundedRect `world:` for `w:`), a duplicate `value:` in Deflate.putBits (meant `count: 2`), and stale names at call sites of seed / string_copy / zeros / abs / pow / hemisphereIrradiance (param renamed n->normal) / rae_str_to_i64 (s->text) / renderDeferredPassWorld / updateDebugOverlay / updateGrassField / uploadMesh / rayColor / describe / allocatorAliveCount.
