- [x] #935 {difficulty:3} [compiler/runtime] `gbReadWgsl` (lib/Gbuffer.rae, over nativeGbReadWgsl -> rae_ext_rae_sys_read_file, a bare `fopen(path, "rb")`) resolves its OWN shader assets by a literal CWD-relative path baked into the stdlib source - `"lib/grass_compute.wgsl"`, `"lib/terrain_palette.wgsl"`, `"lib/underwaterFog.wgsl"`, `"lib/sprite_billboard.wgsl"`, `"lib/transparentForward.wgsl"`, `"lib/world_biome.wgsl"`, `"lib/noise.wgsl"`, `"lib/terrain_detail.wgsl"`, `"lib/terrain_splat.wgsl"`, `"lib/grass_render.wgsl"` across GbufferSprite/GbufferUnderwater/GbufferTerrain/GrassCompute/TransparentForward. #933 made `.rae` MODULE IMPORTS resolve through the toolchain (a downstream project can delete its `lib` symlink and still build - verified by a downstream client), but these ten reads are plain relative-path file opens that #933 never touches, so a project without a physical `lib/` directory at its process cwd compiles clean and then crashes (fopen fails silently, returning an EMPTY string per rae_ext_rae_sys_read_file's own `if (!f) return {NULL,0,0,0}` - the crash is not here, it is whatever downstream WebGPU shader-module creation does with an empty WGSL source, several frames later and much harder to diagnose than a missing file). Two shapes of fix, either closes the gap: (a) resolve these paths through the SAME mechanism `try_resolve_lib_module`/#933's dependency resolver already uses for imports - e.g. join against the toolchain-resolved stdlib dir #933 already computes and records as `dep lib`'s `source`, rather than assuming cwd; or (b) at minimum, fail LOUDLY (a diagnostic naming the missing path) instead of returning an empty string that silently propagates into a WGPU crash far from its cause. Either way this closes the one remaining reason a downstream project must still keep a `lib` symlink/vendor copy after #933 - not for imports, only for these runtime asset reads. Reported by a downstream client after #933; reproduced by building AND RUNNING a project with `lib` deleted entirely (build succeeds, run does not). DONE. Root cause: gbReadWgsl (and NoiseWgsl.source, both extern-aliased to rae_ext_rae_sys_read_file, a bare fopen) read stdlib shaders by cwd-relative "lib/*.wgsl", so a project without a physical lib/ at its process cwd built clean then fed an EMPTY WGSL string into WGPU shader-module creation and crashed frames later. Fix routes all shader-asset reads through a NEW dedicated runtime function rae_ext_rae_gb_read_shader (compiler/runtime/runtime_filesystem.c): (1) tries the path as given so a project lib/ or an assets/ override at cwd still wins; (2) for a "lib/..." path, joins it against $RAE_STDLIB (the toolchain stdlib dir) with the leading "lib/" stripped, so stdlib shaders resolve with no local lib/ — closing the same gap #933 closed for imports; (3) if found nowhere, fails LOUDLY with a stderr diagnostic naming the exact path (and the $RAE_STDLIB tried) instead of returning empty — both fix shapes the task blessed. Wired lib/GbufferNative.rae nativeGbReadWgsl extern("...") and lib/NoiseWgsl.rae externs to the new symbol (covers GbufferSprite/Underwater/Terrain/GrassCompute/TransparentForward/water/* and NoiseWgsl); the generic rae_ext_rae_sys_read_file is untouched so gltf/png/user reads keep their exact empty-on-miss semantics. run_compiled_file and the watch child now setenv("RAE_STDLIB", compiler_stdlib_dir(), 0) (0 = never overwrite a caller value) so `rae run`/`rae watch` are zero-config; the `rae init` Makefile `run` recipe now exports RAE_STDLIB=$(RAE_REPO)/lib for the directly-run built binary. Verified non-visually (NO VISUAL TESTS run) with a scratch program calling the extern: cwd path wins; missing-at-cwd resolves via $RAE_STDLIB; a true miss prints the loud error and returns len 0; and `rae run` with RAE_STDLIB unset resolved lib/noise.wgsl from the real toolchain lib. Full watch-tests.sh suite 511/511 0 failed; edited .rae files verified canonical. No VERSION bump (following the #931-#934 precedent of riding the next release cut rather than moving VERSION mid-slice). Note for the user: a downstream project can now delete its lib symlink/vendor copy entirely — `rae run`/`watch` need nothing; a hand-rolled build+run just needs RAE_STDLIB pointing at the toolchain lib/ (the loud error names it, and `rae init` now sets it). A real GPU render check is a visual gate — please run `make test-examples` by hand if you want to confirm a windowed example still renders.

- [x] #938 {difficulty:3} [gpu/lifetime] `pollSubmission` (lib/gpu/GpuLifetime.rae) misreads `wgpuDevicePoll(wait: 0, submissionIndex)`: per wgpu.h its return value is "true if the QUEUE is empty, false if submissions are still in flight" — not "that index finished". So any consumer that tracks one submission per frame while the renderer keeps the GPU busy never sees its work retire: its `inFlight` list grows by one every frame until the manager's submission slots (capacity 96 in the examples) are full, `submit` returns none, and — for GrassCompute, which resets the indirect draw's instanceCount to 0 BEFORE dispatching — nothing is drawn until the queue happens to drain, at which point every pending submission retires at once and the field comes back. A downstream track-and-field client saw it as grass on for ~10 s, gone for ~2 s, back again; a per-frame probe of `grass.inFlight.length` read 30, 60, 90, 96, 96, 22, 52, 82, 96 — a sawtooth capped at the slot count. Gbuffer/ShadowMaps/Gpu2dCanvasFrame/WaterSystem track submissions the same way and only survive because their polls happen to land when the queue is momentarily empty. Fix: give the runtime a real per-index signal — `rae_wgpu_watch_submission(index)` registers a `wgpuQueueOnSubmittedWorkDone` callback (AllowProcessEvents, index in userdata1, no allocation) that records the highest completed index (indices are monotonic on the one queue), and `rae_wgpu_submission_done(index)` pumps callbacks nonblockingly and answers `index <= highest || queueEmpty`. `submit` watches the index it just got; `pollSubmission` asks the runtime instead of `wgpuDevicePoll`. Also makes the layer work under Emscripten, where `wgpuDevicePoll` does not exist and only the callback path can answer. DONE: runtime_webgpu.c (+ rae_runtime.h prototypes), webgpu/Context.rae externs, GpuLifetime.rae submit/pollSubmission + header comment. Not unit-testable without a device; verified by the downstream client's probe: `inFlight` now stays at 1–2 across a 9 s headless run instead of sawtoothing to 96, and the grass no longer disappears. Full watch-tests.sh suite run after the change (see commit).

Today lib/ui has zero `Schedule` users: 106's FramePipeline and every UI example call fitSystem/layoutSystem/transformSystem/animationSystem/renderSystem in hand order. Extend `addSystem` to take `reads:`/`writes:` table lists (a table id per UiWorld field; `fields(UiWorld)` reflection can enumerate them), make the runner call `shouldRun` off the declared read set instead of a caller-supplied generation, and register every lib/ui system as an entry in its canonical order. Keep behaviour byte-identical (dirty-skip semantics unchanged). This is also the prerequisite for parallel schedule stages (docs/parallelism-first-plan.md Phase 2). Design: docs/ui-ecs-refactor-status.md §2.1, docs/ecs-general-architecture.md ("the schedule is the program"). Verify with watch-tests.sh (full suite green); NO VISUAL TESTS — do not run run_examples.sh / make test-examples / any windowed example; where a look could change, end with a note asking the user to run `make test-examples` for screenshot parity. INVESTIGATED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — blocked by a design fork only you can settle; no code changed. Finding: the authored `.raescene` loader (applyComponentByName + the 35 deserX in RegistryDeser.rae) CANNOT be collapsed by `typeName`/`fields` reflection with today's language, and doing so would silently break scene loading (which I cannot visually verify). Three hard blockers, all confirmed in the maintainer's OWN docs: (1) `docs/compile-time-reflection.md` states "Rae has no field reflection and no function values, so nothing can hold a world's heterogeneous ComponentTable(T) values as data" — so there is NO way to build a name→decoder dispatch table (the "override table, not a ladder" the task asks for is unrepresentable without function values); (2) the same doc: `fields(Type)` CONSTRUCTION was assessed and DECLINED (#774) — reflection is read-only iteration over an existing value, so a generic decoder cannot BUILD a component value field-by-field from JSON; (3) the ONLY generic decoder reflection can reach is the compiler-generated `T.fromJson` (MACHINE format), but the authored grammar is deliberately different — `lib/ui/Serialize.rae`'s own header says the authored loader "parses a hand-friendly grammar (enum strings, theme tokens like \"gap\":\"spaceM\", flat {x,y,w,h}) and STAYS AS-IS ... SEPARATE from" the reflection-driven machine snapshot (worldToJson/worldFromJson, which ALREADY uses fields()+fieldName()). Each deserX applies per-field DEFAULTS for missing keys and enum-string/theme-token/shorthand mapping that fromJson does not — swapping to fromJson would drop those and corrupt every real scene. Reflection thus helps the machine save/load path (done) but not the authored path. Even reflection-deriving just the #941 vocabulary is unsafe: `fields(world)` typeName includes derived/runtime tables (ComputedRect, Parent, WorldTransform2D) that are NOT authorable, and authored-name≠type-name cases exist (authored "Overflow" vs type OverflowPolicy). QUESTION: which direction do you want? (A) Keep the authored loader hand-written (matching the existing Serialize.rae note) and RE-SCOPE #942 to the only safe reflection win — replace the hand-maintained `registeredComponentNames()` list with a reflected, serialize-flag-filtered vocabulary + a small explicit alias table (removes the "name entry" but NOT the decode arms); (B) migrate the `.raescene` authored format to the machine toJson/fromJson format so the existing reflected worldFromJson can load it (a breaking format change across all scene assets + editor tooling, drops the hand-friendly grammar — needs its own design/tasks); or (C) add a language capability (function values / a per-type decoder-registration mechanism / reopen construction reflection) so custom decoders can be dispatched generically (a language-design decision). I recommend (A) for a near-term win but it will NOT collapse the 39 decode arms; (B)/(C) are larger and out of scope for one queue task. RESOLVED / CLOSED — do NOT reopen or re-investigate this item. Maintainer chose (C) scoped narrowly (no function values). This ticket was SPLIT into #959 (mutable field assignment + T.default()), #960 (enumFromName + generic decodeField), and #961 (collapse the arms — the actual re-scoped #942, deps #959/#960/#941). Marked [x] because the work now lives entirely in those three tasks; there is nothing left to do under #942. When #959–#961 are done, this is done — skip it.

INVESTIGATED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — the premise "changedSince over the tables they watch" does not hold; no code changed. Finding: `changedSince`/`componentModStamp` are strictly `ComponentTable(T)`-scoped (per-entity denseStamps / table generation). But 106's three bespoke counters observe RESOURCE/ACTOR state, NOT component tables: `historyLen` watches `state.playHistory.entries.length` (a plain `List(PlayHistoryEntry)` on the AppState resource), `sheetEpoch` watches `state.bottomSheet.epoch` (an Int field on the BottomSheetState resource), and `playbackRevision`/`nowPlayingRevision` watch `PlaybackState.revision`/`.nowPlayingRevision` — PlaybackState IS the design's PlaybackSystem ACTOR (§3/§5.1) and those are its component-INSTANCE / SYSTEM revisions (§7). None of PlayHistory / BottomSheetState / PlaybackState is a ComponentTable, so there is no table generation for changedSince to read. Crucially the observation doc's OWN model (ecs-systems-and-data-observation.md §7) has THREE revision levels: TABLE revision = componentTableGeneration/changedSince; SYSTEM revision = a bespoke `revision: Int`; component-INSTANCE revision = a bespoke `revision: Int` field — i.e. the doc EXPLICITLY blesses the exact bespoke ints 106 uses for its non-table state (the code even cites §7). And 106 ALREADY uses the table-level primitive where it applies: RenderCacheGpu2d.rae keys its dirty check off `componentTableGeneration` over ComputedRect/WorldTransform2D/Shape/Sprite/Text/Active/Opacity/Children/Parent/OnClick. So "0 uses of changedSince in the example" is only true of these resource observers, which are not changedSince candidates. To delete these counters and use changedSince, 106's playback / play-history / bottom-sheet state would have to be RE-MODELLED as ECS component tables (entities) — a substantial data-model refactor, visually-untestable here, and at odds with the doc framing PlaybackState as a resource/actor. QUESTION: which direction? (A) CLOSE as not-applicable / already-correct — accept that these are the doc §7 system/instance-revision pattern (table-level observation is already done in RenderCacheGpu2d), optionally with a tiny tidy of `historyLen` from a List-length diff into a named revision int (still not changedSince); (B) commission a separate, larger task to re-model 106's playback/history/bottom-sheet as ECS component tables so table-level `changedSince`/`componentModStamp` applies and the revision ints disappear (its own difficulty-4+ effort, needs screenshot verification); or (C) something else. I recommend (A). Guessing wrong (re-architecting the data model, or ripping out the revisions and breaking observation in an example I cannot run) would waste the work — hence asking rather than implementing. RESOLVED: maintainer chose (A) — close as already-correct + do the tidy. DONE: added `revision: Int` to `PlayHistory` (createPlayHistory inits 0), bumped on every append (recordPlay + restoreHistoryFromSource), and switched `refreshHistoryViewsIfNeeded` to observe `playHistory.revision` instead of diffing `entries.length` (renamed the observe cache `UiRefreshCache.historyLen`->`historyRevision` + its createUiRefreshCache param + the Main.rae seed/sync sites). Behaviour-preserving (append bumps revision exactly where the length used to grow) and strictly more correct at cap (an append that evicts leaves length unchanged but bumps revision). `sheetEpoch` and `playbackRevision`/`nowPlayingRevision` left as-is — they are the doc §7 system/instance-revision pattern for resource/actor state, not changedSince candidates. - [x] #965 {difficulty:5} It seems like all examples, such as 106 and 114 at least, leak memory like hell while just being idle. Crazy. Even crazier that none of our tests have caught this happening during the refactorings. Do not revert anything. But investigate the leaks, analyze reasons and DO PROPER fixes. Not hacky fixes of any kind. Robust, production ready, sane fixes to the memory leaks. You can even change language or the compiler, if their design is causing the leaks. DONE. Measured first (RSS sampling + RAE_MEM_STATS per-site + macOS `leaks` with MallocStackLogging on a -g build): 114 windowed idle grew ~48 MB/s (162k leaked List buffers in 12 s, every stack through Gpu2dCanvas.emptyTextAtlas -> createList), and 106 with Spotify ON sat at 2.4 GB RSS (26k leaked `concat` strings = 2.1 GB, one JSON save of the play history) plus a slow interp leak per poll tick; headless 106 / Spotify-off were flat, which is why the gates never saw it (they run headless, no Spotify, no windowed idle loop). Root causes are three COMPILER ownership gaps, fixed in codegen (no example was touched): (1) a whole-value store into an owned heap-owning place — local, field, element, or through a `mod T` param — never released the previous value (`var atlas = emptyTextAtlas(); atlas = own known` leaked four Lists per glyph); now the RHS is evaluated into a temp, the old value dropped (unless the local was moved out), then installed — c_stmt.c assignment for both the owned-place and the `mod`-ref paths, String included (pool_take on fresh strings). (2) `own <member>` was a pass-through leaving the source live; with (1) that double-freed the swap idiom (EventQueue.frameAdvance) — now `own <place>` reads the value out and zeroes the source (the valid empty value), a `let` from a move owns, and `List/IntMap/StringMap.drop()` leave data null instead of dangling (fixture 417's contract). (3) a fresh String (call/interp/concat result) borrowed by a `view String` param was hoisted into an `__rae_pw` temp and never dropped — every intermediate of a chained `.concat()` leaked; now such slots are #884 statement temporaries (pool-taken, dropped after the statement); and a String local reassigned from a fresh value is marked owning so its scope exit releases it (`var s: String = ""` at function top leaked once per call). After: 114 buf outstanding 162,369 -> 19 (constant boot residue, flat between 6 s and 20 s runs), 106+Spotify RSS 2.4 GB -> ~180 MB with interp/concat outstanding 7/0 and flat over 34 s; 114 windowed RSS 183 -> 186 MB over 30 s decelerating — that residual is outside Rae's allocator (GPU/Metal pools, not attributable this turn). Regression guard: fixture 847 (all three patterns, RAE_MEM_STATS outstanding delta < 100 over 3000 rounds; added to run_tests.sh's mem-stats list). Docs: docs/drop-semantics-and-defer.md gets the decided assignment rules. VERSION 0.3.1 -> 0.3.2. Verified: watch-tests.sh 494/494 (one round caught 417's explicit-drop contract, fixed in lib), visual gates 106/112/114 PASS. Follow-up filed: #971.

Add boxing for POD/String-owning struct payloads: the ring stores an owned copy of T (deep-copied on send, moved out on receive, dropped with the channel on free), keeping MPSC, the no-blocking-receive rule and the Int fast path; the C backend must specialise the ring element size/copy/drop per T the way List does. Runtime: `RaeChannel` is a byte ring of `cap * elemSize` (`rae_ext_rae_chan_new(elemSize)`), and the C side only hands out slot INDICES under its mutex — `reserve`/`commit` (producer) and `take`/`release` (consumer, zeroes the slot) — while the typed store/load stays in Rae: `channelSend(value: own T)` moves the value into the slot with `rae_ext_rae_buf_set` over the ring exposed as `Buffer(T)` (`rae_ext_rae_chan_ring`), `receive` moves it out with `rae_ext_rae_buf_get` + `ret own val`, `freeChannel` drains and drops what is still buffered before freeing — the same per-T specialisation List uses, so Int is the same code with an 8-byte slot (no separate fast path needed), MPSC and no-blocking-receive unchanged, full ring still refuses the send. - [x] #970 {difficulty:3} [compiler/sema] A method call on an UNDECLARED identifier passes sema and only fails in gcc. Repro: `import Time` then `let seconds: Float64 = now.epochSeconds()` with no `now` in scope — `rae build --emit-c` succeeds and emits `rae_epochSeconds()`; the C compiler reports "call to undeclared function". Found in #950 (a removed `now` parameter left a `now.epochSeconds()` behind and the Rae build still passed). Sema must resolve the receiver of a UFCS/method call like any other identifier and report `unknown identifier 'now'` at the Rae source position; add a compile-error fixture. Check the sibling forms too (`now.field`, `now[0]`, `now as Float`). Deps: none. Verify with watch-tests.sh (full suite green). DONE. Root cause: sema analyzed a UFCS/method-call and `.member` receiver in NON-value position (to let a module/type qualifier through), so a bare-ident receiver that named no value — a since-removed parameter (`now.epochSeconds()`, the #950 case), or a bare function name — left resolved_type NULL, the method-resolution block was skipped, and the C backend emitted a bare `rae_epochSeconds()` that only gcc rejected. Fix (compiler/src/sema.c): (1) in the IDENT value-position handler a resolved FUNCTION symbol is now an error (functions are not first-class values in Rae) — covers the sibling forms `now as Float`, `now[0]`, and interpolation `"{now}"`, which are already analyzed in value position; (2) after analyzing a method-call/`.member` receiver, a new `sema_report_bad_receiver` reports a bare-ident receiver that resolves to no value and to no FUNCTION either, at the receiver's own line:col — with the "names a function" message for a function symbol and the existing "unknown value" message for a truly-undeclared name. It deliberately does NOT flag a module/type/enum namespace, a generic parameter (decl-less symbol), a primitive-type namespace, or a `__`-intrinsic; a new `sema_name_is_module_component` recognizes lib/subfolder/imported/project-folder module qualifiers (case-insensitive, so the PascalCase folder form `Particles.tick()` is accepted) which sema leaves for the backend to resolve. - [x] #971 {difficulty:3} [examples/114+lib/ui] 114 churns ~140k List buffers per second while idle (RAE_MEM_STATS: 2.8M buf allocs in 20 s, all balanced after #965 — not a leak, but 2.4 GB of malloc/free traffic for an idle frame loop) and its windowed RSS still creeps ~0.1 MB/s decelerating (183 -> 186 MB over 30 s) with Rae-level allocations flat, i.e. outside Rae's allocator. Two parts: (a) find the per-frame scratch Lists (macOS `leaks`/`malloc_history` or RAE_MEM_STATS deltas per system; candidates: gpu2d text batching `emptyTextAtlas` copies per glyph — the `var atlas = emptyTextAtlas(); if let known = copyAt {...}` copy-mutate-set pattern deep-copies the whole atlas (glyph List) per glyph — plus render-graph/uniform scratch) and make them persistent per-frame buffers (`modAt` in place instead of copyAt+set); (b) attribute the residual RSS creep with `vmmap`/`heap` over a 2-minute windowed run (Metal drawable / wgpu pool warm-up vs a real C-level leak) and fix or document. Verify with RAE_MEM_STATS cumulative alloc counts (docs/parallel-tests.md style) + a 60 s RSS sample; watch-tests.sh green. DONE (part a: the identified O(n^2) driver; part b: attributed). MEASURED first with RAE_MEM_STATS on a headless 18 s run: baseline buf alloc=2,847,728 (2.4 GB traffic), outstanding=19 (confirmed not a leak). ROOT of the churn: `canvasDrawGlyphEx` (lib/Gpu2dCanvasText.rae) runs ONCE PER GLYPH and used the copy-mutate-set anti-pattern — `var entry = emptyTextAtlas(); if let known = copyAt(ai) { entry = own known }; entry.glyphs.add(...); set(ai, own entry)` — so every glyph DEEP-COPIED the whole already-accumulated glyph List (O(n^2) per frame, a fresh Buffer per glyph). FIX: append in place through a `mod` window (`if let entry: mod Gpu2dTextAtlas => canvas.textAtlases.modAt(index: ai)`), no per-glyph copy/alloc. Applied the same copyAt+set -> modAt conversion to the other per-frame/per-flush whole-atlas copies that deep-copied the (large) glyph List for a trivial mutation: `clearTextBatches`, `clearTextBatch`, `ensureTextAtlas`, `textFlushBuffer` (all only mutate `resources`, never `canvas`, between get and set, so an in-place window is safe), and `boxFrameEnd`'s flush-cursor reset loop (Gpu2dCanvasFrame.rae). AFTER: buf alloc 2,847,728 -> 1,791,821 (-37%), traffic 2.4 GB -> 1.08 GB (-55%), outstanding still 19. Part (b): 60 s headless RSS sample climbs 183 -> 190 MB and PLATEAUS from ~t=30 s (flat 190 through t=55 s) while Rae buf outstanding stays 19 — a decelerating warm-up that stabilises (wgpu/Metal pool + buffer growth), NOT a C-level leak; matches #965's windowed finding and the drs-memory-leak note. The residual per-frame churn (~1.79M/18s) is now the renderer's per-pass bind-group descriptor Lists (`List(ResourceRef)` rebuilt every draw across ~20 GbufferPasses/ShadowMaps/Gpu2dCanvas* sites) — a broad, separate concern (and arguably a bind-group-caching question), split out as #973 rather than half-done here. - [x] #973 {difficulty:3} [lib/ui+renderer] Per-frame bind-group scratch Lists. After #971 fixed the gpu2d text O(n^2) glyph churn, 114's remaining idle malloc/free traffic (~1.79M Buffer alloc+free / 18 s headless, all balanced — not a leak) is dominated by the renderer rebuilding a fresh `List(ResourceRef)` per draw call / per pass every frame: ~20 sites (lib/GbufferPasses.rae, GbufferSprite/Skinned/Sdf/Terrain/Underwater/Inspector.rae, ShadowMaps*.rae, GrassCompute.rae, Gpu2dCanvas.rae:799, Gpu2dCanvasImage.rae:505, Gpu2dCanvasText.rae:358 `entries`, plus textFlushAtlas's per-flush `batch` copyAt). Reduce the traffic: either (a) reuse a persistent per-frame scratch `List(ResourceRef)` (clear+refill instead of create) threaded on the resources/canvas, or (b) cache the bind groups themselves by (pipeline, entry-ids) key so the descriptor list is built once, not per frame — decide which. Not a correctness bug (outstanding is flat); this is allocator-traffic/perf. Verify with RAE_MEM_STATS cumulative buf alloc counts on a headless 114 run (target: well under the current 1.79M/18s) + watch-tests.sh green; visual gate 114 + one 3D example. DONE — but the task's stated target (bind-group ResourceRef lists) turned out to be a MINOR contributor. MEASURED with a temporary env-gated return-address histogram in rae_ext_rae_buf_alloc (added, used, removed) on a headless 114 run: baseline 1.876M buf allocs / 18 s. Bind-group `List(ResourceRef)`/`List(WGPUBindGroupEntry)` were only ~18k combined. The real per-frame churn was four sites, all now fixed: (1) `GpuArgs.pushF32` allocated a 1-element `List(Float)` scratch per call to reinterpret a float to bytes (~500k allocs) — replaced with a new `rae_ext_rae_f32_bits` reinterpret intrinsic + `appendWord`, no heap; (2) `GltfSkin.nodeWorldMatrix` allocated a `chain: List(Int)` per joint per frame (~486k) — rewritten to walk parent->root pre-multiplying `local(cur) * acc` (Mat4 is a value Array, so mat4Mul allocates nothing), same product, no list; (3) `layoutSystem.activeChildren` allocated a fresh `List(EntityId)` per node per frame in measureNode + placeChildren (~185k) — added `activeChildrenInto(out:)` filling a REUSED scratch threaded from the flat measure/place drivers (layout is a non-reentrant linear walk, so one buffer per phase is safe); (4) `textFlushWith` did `copyAt` of the WHOLE atlas (4 Lists) for EVERY atlas EVERY frame just to read `glyphClips.length` (~124/frame) — changed to a `view` window. RESULT: 1.876M -> 230,843 buf allocs (-88%), 1.13 GB -> 234 MB traffic, outstanding still 19 (no leak, as before). Remaining small sites (imageFlushWith image batch, textFlushAtlas per-flush `batch` copyAt, the actual bind-group entries ~8k) are per-flush not per-frame and blocked on the canvas mod/view aliasing rule — left as-is (diminishing returns; a persistent bind-group cache is a separate design). - [x] #982 {difficulty:2} [compiler] A .rae file over the 1,000-line cap HANGS the compiler instead of failing: `rae format --check lib/ui/Components.rae` at 1014 lines spun until the alarm (SIGALRM), and `rae build` died with `arena_alloc: out of space (request=32, used=67108864, cap=67108864)` in `parser_alloc` (found in #978). The cap is documented as a refusal ("a canonical form over 1,000 lines is REFUSED, never written" / "an error to split"), so the format preflight or the parser must report `file exceeds 1000 lines: split it` at the file's position and exit non-zero — no retry loop, no arena exhaustion. Add a fixture with a 1,001-line file expecting that diagnostic. Verify with watch-tests.sh. DONE. ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by direct repro: the lexer's own 1000-line hard cap (lexer.c, predates this task) already stops tokenization cleanly and reports `file exceeds the hard cap of 1000 lines` — that part never hung. The bug was downstream in `rae_format_source` (used by BOTH `rae format --check` and the `rae build` preflight, lib/ui/Ecs.rae's `module_graph_load_module`): it called `parse_module` UNCONDITIONALLY on the token stream even when the lexer had already flagged it broken (`tokens.had_error`), instead of short-circuiting the way `main.c`'s `parse`/`lex` commands already did. Parser error-recovery over that leftover/truncated token stream could cascade into a large number of diagnostics and allocations in the function's private 64MB arena — matching the reported `arena_alloc: out of space (... cap=67108864) in parser_alloc` crash; a big-enough cascade (confirmed with a synthetic 1001-line file of unfixed-type `let`s: 999 cascaded errors) is the same class of bug that likely hung under different content. FIX (compiler/src/rae_format.c): (1) check `input_lines > 1000` FIRST, before creating any arena or touching the lexer/parser at all — an O(n) line count that cannot hang, refusing with `<path> has <N> lines: file exceeds 1000 lines, split it into smaller modules`, reusing the existing `over_cap` field/reporting path (same one the post-format output-cap check already used); (2) added a `tokens.had_error` short-circuit before `parse_module` as defense in depth for any OTHER lexer-flagged breakage, not just the line cap. Verified via direct repro: reconstructing the actual over-cap Components.rae+BindingComponents.rae content (1093 lines) through `format --check` AND through `rae build --emit-c --project examples/106_mobile_ui` both now fail instantly and cleanly instead of hanging/crashing. Fixture: NEW `compiler/tests/cases/850_format_check_over_cap` (1001-line valid-syntax file, `format --check`, expects the new diagnostic + exit 1) — the pre-existing `390_long_file_error` already covered the default `parse` command's message but nothing exercised the format/preflight path specifically. Also fixed `format-check-tree.sh`: its over-cap check fired unconditionally (even under tests/cases/), which would have failed the tree check on 390 and the new 850 fixture now that they report `overCap` instead of a generic parse error — folded over-cap into the same tests/cases/-tolerant branch as parse errors (a REAL over-cap file under lib/ or examples/ still fails the gate; verified by transiently growing lib/ui/Components.rae past 1000 lines and confirming format-check-tree.sh catches it). watch-tests.sh 497/497 (496 + the new fixture), format-check-tree PASS (954 files canonical).

Found 2026-09-15 while migrating game-proto3 to Rae #943 (a `UiInput` was passed for a `world: UiWorld` parameter; the only symptom was a runtime SIGSEGV). Related, same family: named args are positional (memory: emit-c accepts a wrong ORDER, only gcc catches it) — cover that in the same fixtures if it is not already. DONE. Root cause was one place in `resolve_function_overload` (compiler/src/sema.c): for a non-generic candidate whose argument TYPES mismatched it set `mismatch`, and because an open name+arity candidate existed NONE of the diagnostic branches fired — it returned NULL silently and the C backend re-resolved the call by name and emitted it anyway; gcc only WARNS on an incompatible struct pointer, which is exactly why A/B/C compiled, linked and ran. The per-argument checks already existed (`ensure_type_match` names distinct structs since #414 and scalar kinds since #959; `sema_check_call_arg_names` checks names) but only run on a BOUND decl. Fix: (1) bind the SOLE open non-generic arity candidate on ANY argument mismatch (generalising #410's numeric-only shortcut) so both checks run at the argument — A/B now `cannot convert Apple to Basket; they are different types`, D `type mismatch: expected Int, got String`, C reports the name error AND the type error independently; a swapped order (E) reports the name error plus a type error at each argument; (2) when several open overloads take this arity and none accepts the types, a new `no overload of 'f' accepts these argument types; the candidates taking N arguments are: <signatures>` diagnostic at the call, instead of the backend picking one by name. Both are guarded by `!open_generic_candidate`: a generic call the resolver cannot infer (e.g. `contains(this: xs, value: 3)` on a List(Int), whose only non-generic namesake is String.contains) is legitimately bound by name in the backend — the first cut mis-diagnosed exactly that (389_list_helpers) and the guard fixed it. Fixtures 851-857 (struct/view, struct/mod, wrong name+type, scalar, wrong ORDER, no-overload-matches, and a passing control incl. a resolved overload set). Verified: full suite 504 passed, 0 failed; ALL 76 examples still emit-c; end-to-end gates 104/106/94/96/116/120/zz_gpu_args_check PASS. Only compiler/src/sema.c + the 7 fixtures changed.

An app that fills the G-buffer through its own draws (skinned / instanced / procedural / grass between beginPass and endPass, never the World3d mesh query) is therefore forced to carry an EMPTY second World3d purely as a type-shaped argument — 114_walker_character's `emptyWorld` field, seven call sites, and a `createWorld3d()` nobody reads. Fix: split the entry. New pub `renderDeferredPass(renderer, tag, camera, light, aspect)` runs every scene-independent tag (gbuffer is a deliberate no-op there); `renderDeferredPassWorld` keeps its signature, does the gbuffer branch itself and delegates every other tag to `renderDeferredPass`; the internal `renderDeferredPassWith` loses its `world` parameter. No caller of renderDeferredPassWorld changes. Rae has NO argv API: the C backend emits `int main(int argc, char** argv) { (void)argc; (void)argv; ... }` (compiler/src/c_backend.c:~1530) and `rae run` never forwards anything to the child. Also `rae build --emit-c` apps: the copied runtime must carry the seam (runtime_system_log.c or a new small runtime_args.c included by rae_runtime.c — and mind the Makefile .d rule, #989). Verify: a fixture `compiler/tests/cases/NNN_program_args` whose expected output prints `argCount` and each arg for `-- a "b c"`; `rae run` with no `--` prints 0; full suite green. DONE. Runtime: new runtime/runtime_args.c (included by rae_runtime.c after runtime_system_log.c; auto-copied by the runtime_*.c rule, picked up by the #989 .d rule) holds argv[1..] via rae_runtime_set_args(argc, argv), which the emitted main now calls instead of voiding argc/argv; rae_ext_rae_sys_arg_count / rae_ext_rae_sys_arg_at behind lib/Sys.rae argCount() / argAt(index) (empty string out of range or negative). CLI: parse_run_args stops at the first `--` (RunOptions.app_argc/app_argv), run_compiled_file spawns the binary with fork+execv (no shell, so `"b c"` stays one arg) instead of system(), watch_spawn_child forwards the same argv on every restart, toolchain_check's --check-toolchain scan stops at `--`, `rae run --help` documents it. Test runner: config.cmd `run -- a "b c"` re-parses the line with shell quoting and puts the entry file BEFORE the `--`. Fixtures 858_program_args (prints argCount + each arg + out-of-range) and 859_program_args_none (no `--` -> 0). Verified: both fixtures pass, a `rae build --emit-c` project compiles standalone and sees the OS argv as-is, `rae watch ... -- w1 "w 2"` prints the args, full suite 506 passed / 0 failed.

Design (agreed 2026-09-15): (a) a scene reference is a PACKAGE PATH WITHOUT EXTENSION, `folder/SubFolder/SceneName` — PascalCase scene files/ids, camelCase folders, exactly the Rae module rule; used by BOTH the new top-level `"import": ["Theme", "shared/GameAssets"]` and the existing `SceneInstance.sceneId` (`"cards/HeroCard"`; today's bare `"CoverageCard"` is the zero-folder case, unchanged). The extension is a property of the file, never of the reference (the format can be renamed later). Binary data (`.png`, `.mtsdf.json`) is the opposite: a string FILE path WITH extension, relative to the declaring scene file — the AGENTS.md data-vs-module distinction. (b) A SCENE ROOT, mirroring `rae run`: package paths resolve from the directory of the scene that was OPENED (the entry scene), overridable by `--scene-root <dir>` / `RAE_UI_EDITOR_ROOT` in the viewer and passed explicitly by apps that mount from Rae code (the loader already takes a directory). No walking up for a `.raepack`, no magic files. Sub-scene resolution therefore changes from relative-to-parent-folder to relative-to-root (shipped samples are flat: unaffected). (c) `import` brings a scene's CONFIGURATION into scope — its `assets` block and the theme token blocks (palette/space/radius/text styles) — mounting nothing (mounting stays `SceneInstance`), like a Rae `import` makes declarations available without running anything; no `open` (there is no qualified/bare distinction for tokens). Transitive through the same SceneRegistry (cycle-checked, depth-capped with a diagnostic); resolution is nearest-wins in list order: the scene's own blocks, then each import depth-first, first declaration of a token / texture key / font wins; a `SceneInstance` child resolves through its own file + imports, then the mounting page's resolved set. (d) `"assets": { "textures": { "dirs": ["../textures"], "map": { "menu.playButton": "../art/Play_Button.png" } }, "fonts": { "text": "../fonts/ChelaOne-Regular.mtsdf.json", "icons": "..." } }` allowed in ANY scene; `map` = key->file, `dirs` = `<dir>/<key>.png`, lookup map -> dirs -> imports; NO manifest-of-Rae-source (a .raescene never parses .rae; a project with a Rae manifest generates the map). Fonts are world-level in v1: first `fonts` declaration wins, a conflicting later one is a diagnostic (per-node fonts = renderer change, separate). `SdfText.loadSdfFont` accepts the sibling atlas as `.png` OR `.raw`. (e) THE THEME AUTO-LOAD OF `<dir>/theme.raescene` IS REMOVED in the same change — a scene writes `"import": ["Theme"]`; migrate every shipped scene (121 samples, lib/app3d/scenes, examples 105/106/111/112/...; `theme.raescene` -> `Theme.raescene`) and make a scene that still relies on the old auto-load get a diagnostic naming the file it should import; the in-file `"sceneId"` becomes a checked assertion against the path (mismatch = diagnostic) — to be dropped in a later version. - [x] #1010 {difficulty:3} [lib/core + sema] `List.copyAtDefault` / `copyAtFallback` on a `List(String)` (and any heap-carrying T) return `rae_ext_rae_buf_get`'s SHALLOW alias: the caller's binding owns nothing yet is dropped, freeing the list's buffer (found in #1008: `sceneAssetTexturePath` crashed at exit via drop_struct_SceneAssets -> List_drop_String until it used `copyAt` + `if let`, whose unwrap deep-copies). Either make the two total accessors deep-copy like copyAt's unwrap (the #899 rule), or extend the #881 list-accessor sema check to reject them for heap types with a pointer to copyAt/viewAt. Fixture with a List(String) read through both, exit 0. DONE (option 1 — deep-copy in the accessor, not the sema-rejection option). Root cause confirmed: both bodies did `ret rae_ext_rae_buf_get(this.data, index)`, returning a String whose `.data` pointer aliased the element's own heap; the C backend's alias-return classifier (rae_func_returns_alias) hid it for simple `let x = list.copyAtDefault(i)` callers (marks x is_owned=0, skips the drop), but the moment the value escaped into a durably-owned place (added to another List, stored in a struct field that outlives the source, returned up a non-alias path) it was owned and dropped while the source list still owned the same buffer -> double free (drop_struct -> List_drop -> str_free of a freed pointer, the #1008 SceneImports crash). NOTE the bug only bites HEAP elements: a String LITERAL has a static buffer whose double-drop is a silent no-op, so it only reproduces with interpolated/heap strings. Fix: rewrote copyAtDefault/copyAtFallback to delegate to `copyAt` (`if let value: T = copyAt(this, index: index) { ret value }` then the fallback/default), so the in-range result rides copyAt's #899 optional-payload deep-copy (rae_string_copy / rae_deep_copy_<T>) and comes back an OWNED, independent value. As a bonus the two are no longer classified alias-returning (the ret is a copyAt-derived if-let binding, not a raw buf_get), so callers now correctly own+drop them. PODs (Int/Float/BufferId — the ~140 existing callers are almost all POD) are unaffected: copyAt of a POD is a plain read, no copy machinery. Chose option 1 over the sema-reject because copyAtDefault/copyAtFallback on `List(String)` is exactly what #1007/#1008 wanted (parallel texturePaths etc.) and the 'copy' name + the family doc already promise a deep copy. Fixture 865_list_copy_default_heap reads a List(String) of heap strings through BOTH accessors, escaping into an independently-owned list plus out-of-range default/fallback; FAILS (abort) on the old bodies, PASSES (exit 0) with the fix. Verified: full unit suite 512/0 (was 511; +865), all copyAtDefault/copyAtFallback callers across lib+examples still green; 121 Coverage headless mounts 0 diagnostics exit 0. sema untouched — the '[lib/core + sema]' tag anticipated the reject route; the deep-copy route needed lib/core only.

Two shapes in the curve: a steady ~6-8 MB/s ramp, plus step jumps of ~450 MB and ~830 MB at roughly 40-60 s intervals (allocator growth, or a large periodic copy). The wgpu object counts are FLAT the whole run ([wgpu-report] buf=56 tex=31 texView=98 bind=112/113 at frame 0 and frame 24360), so it is not GPU objects leaking through the manager — it is CPU-side: suspects in order — the FftSurfaceCache / WaterReadback path (per-frame readback of a 256x256 RGBA16F cascade = 512 KB, staged into Rae Lists per snapshot: is the previous snapshot's List dropped?), the spray emitter's per-snapshot burst lists (#859), per-frame `List.create` in waterDraw/uploadFftUniform (`evolveUniform` floats, `commands`) that are never dropped because a `let` list from a call result is not auto-dropped (see the c_backend_internal.h local_struct_owns_heap note), and the string pool if a per-frame log/interp escapes. Method: bisect by disabling one subsystem at a time under the same 180 s run (RAE_WATER_SPRAY=0, buoyancy off, readback off, SSR off) and watch which one flattens the curve; then fix the owner. Verify: RSS flat (±50 MB) over a 3-minute headless run at 3x256; 119 gate green. Sequenced LAST after the other open fixes on purpose (user's call, 2026-09-16). DONE. Root cause was the App-owned GpuResources dependency arena: every FFT, readback and surface submission appended its recorded dependency triples, and water retired completed submissions but never called the existing relocating compactor. Native WebGPU object counts therefore stayed flat while three CPU Lists grew each frame and doubled capacity in large RSS steps. Generated C confirmed the suspected per-frame raw/readback and compute-command Lists are auto-dropped. waterPollSubmissions now compacts after retirement, preserving slices owned by live bind groups, submissions and readbacks; the 119 tier gate asserts that the arena remains bounded. Reproduced the old build at 1,337 -> 2,873 MB RSS in 70 s. The fixed 3x256 build stayed within 828..921 MB over the complete 180 s sample (within +/-50 MB around the centre) and was flat at 914..921 MB for the final 50 s. The focused 119 hardware gate passed 1/0.

Fixed by comparing the desired order against a `view`-read snapshot and taking the `mod` borrow only when it actually changed — a genuine idle busy-relayout eliminated app-wide (every flow ListView benefits, incl. 121). With `childrens`/`computedRects` now STABLE at idle, added `computedRects` to the `progress` observation row's declared reads (observeSystem/AppObservation) — the honest declaration the brief asked for — so the row re-runs once the player page is laid out and the fill width is real, without re-running every idle frame. - [x] #11773361 {difficulty:4} [compiler — `match let`: unwrap an `opt T` and match it in one statement] The opt-shaped twin of `if let`, for what a lookup returns (`enumFromName(Kind, name: text)` is `opt Kind`; any find/parse returning `opt Enum`): `match let kind: Kind = lookup(...) { case Kind.small { ... } case Kind.large { ... } case none { ... } }`. Rules, all following from what exists: the binding is written with its type on the left exactly like `if let` (no inference); the `none` arm is spelled with the existing literal `none` (no new keyword) and is REQUIRED for an opt subject — leaving it out is the same compile error as a missing enum member; an enum subject still forbids `default` (#621) and must name every member; an Int/String/struct subject requires `default` as today and `default` does NOT cover `none` (none is always its own arm, so a reader sees the absent case). The bound name is in scope in every value arm, not in the `none` arm. `match let` is ONLY for an `opt T` subject — the `let` IS the unwrap; on a non-opt subject it is a compile error ('the subject is not an opt; use match'), exactly as `if let` on a non-opt is meaningless. A plain `match` never has a `case none` (its subject cannot be absent); a `match let` always must — the subject's TYPE decides the arm list, the same rule `default` already follows. Lowers like `if let` + `match` (an if/else chain — no C switch), so ownership/drop semantics are the existing ones (#623). Parser: `match` followed by `let` takes the `if let` binding grammar; sema: the exhaustiveness check gains the `none` arm; formatter: same layout as `match`. Fixtures: an enum subject (all members + none, and the errors for a missing none / a missing member / a stray default), an Int subject (default + none), the bound name usable in arms, and a nested `match let` inside a `loop`. Docs: docs/match-and-sum-types.md gets a section (it lists the audited constructs) and docs/compile-time-reflection.md's enumFromName example uses it. No parentheses, same brace blocks as `if` / `match`. Bump compiler/VERSION PATCH. — DONE (0.1.50): `match let name: T = <opt>` implemented end to end. Parser takes the `if let` binding grammar after `match`; sema validates the two rules that are the construct's own (subject must be an opt; `case none` REQUIRED) and then REWRITES the statement into `if let name: T = e { match name { value arms } } else { none arm }`, so ownership/drop (#623), enum exhaustiveness, the no-`default`-on-enum rule (#621) and the `default`-required-on-Int/String rule are all the existing checks unchanged — and `default` cannot cover `none` because the none arm is lifted out before that check. A plain `match` now rejects `case none`. The rewrite is in SEMA, not the parser, because the formatter renders the AST: `rae format` never runs sema, so `match let` round-trips its source shape (verified idempotent). An enum member literally named `none` (`LayoutType.none`) stays distinct from `case none` — pinned in the fixture. Fixtures 891 (enum + or-patterns + Int default/none + bound name in arms + nested in a loop + member-named-none) and 892 (all five diagnostics). Docs: new section in docs/match-and-sum-types.md + the enumFromName example in docs/compile-time-reflection.md.

The only consumer iterates the whole thing once per document (re)load and registers each entry; the keyed structure ALREADY EXISTS downstream as the SceneRegistry (`sceneRegistryIndex(reg:, key:)`), so a Map here would be a second index of the same data that can drift from it, and it would throw away the deterministic registration order a List gives for free. The real fix is to make the two manglers AGREE on enum/Int-newtype elements program-wide (one canonical spelling) — either both keep the enum name (needs a distinct toString) or both erase to int64 (loses member names in a List(enum).toString). So a reveal that needs more than one viewport of scroll destroys the panel, which is why it was not shipped. Investigate the virtual path's translation model: `listViewSyncEntity` sets a `RuntimeOffset` on the LIST itself (its comment calls the scroll `a runtime translation of the whole list`), while `Overflow: Clip` also sits on that same TreeList node, so the clip window appears to travel with the content it is meant to clip. Note 106's only virtual list (`Body` in History.raescene) has NO Overflow on the list or its parent, so this combination may simply never have been exercised. Decide the model — clip on a fixed-size parent with a tall inner content node (the ScrollRoot shape), or make the renderer apply a node's clip in layout space before its RuntimeOffset — then re-add the editor call at the end of `syncTreePanel` (a `lastRevealed: EntityId` on InspectorSystem so it fires only when the active node CHANGES, or every panel sync yanks the list back and manual scrolling becomes impossible). Field writes through such a binding (`slot.label = ...`) work; only the whole-value `slot = value` store is broken. Found while writing fixture 918 (the `=` copies rule), which tests the plain `let slot: mod T => place` form instead. Fix: in the if-let narrowing, give the bound `mod T`/`view T` its NON-opt pointee type for the store path (c_stmt.c AST_STMT_ASSIGN `is_mod_ref` branch, `pointee.is_opt`), then apply the same `=` copies / `own` moves rule there; add the modAt form to 918. — DONE: two fixes. (1) The store path (c_stmt.c AST_STMT_ASSIGN `is_mod_ref`): a whole-value store THROUGH a `mod` reference is always through a narrowed one — an optional reference cannot be stored through without an `if let` first — so the pointee is now the plain T whatever `opt` the binding's declared type still carries; that covers every narrowing path at once (`modAt`, the map's `modGet`, any future accessor) and the previous task's `!pointee.is_opt` guard is gone, so the `=` copies / `own` moves rule applies there too. (2) The `if let … => xs.modAt(index:)` fast path (emit_list_if_let) now registers the binding's local under its narrowed (non-opt) type, the truthful one inside the branch. Fixture 918 grew `assignThroughModAt`, `assignStringThroughModAt` and `assignThroughModGet` (StringMap): values read back right, outstanding allocations back to baseline; the pre-task compiler fails the fixture with `initializing 'RaeAny' with … 'rae_Holder'`. (The `mod String` modAt store already worked after #79484806 via the primitive-mod-ref path; verified.) Full suite 569/569, every example compiles, 121/106/114 windowed gates pass. Version 0.1.79.

It is NOT the outline drawing: each hover change makes inspectorUpdate call syncTreePanel (inspectorSystem/Panels.rae), which rebuilds every hierarchy row, and that rebuild leaks Strings every time. MEASUREMENT (10-minute headless memory test, MainMenu, pointer alternating Title <-> OrbitPlanet every frame, idle editor alongside as control): 103,500 hovers, each a painted frame; Strings never freed at exit 1,457,854 (control: 8,630); List/buffer allocations never freed 114 in BOTH (no List leak); physical footprint at 9.5 min 153.5 MB vs 96.9 MB idle; RSS rose ~4 MB/min for the first 7 min, then flattened only because macOS began compressing pages (the idle control dropped 126 -> 85 MB at the same moment), so RSS alone under-reports it. A separate 25 s run with MallocStackLogging=1 + `leaks <pid>`: 33,143 leaked blocks after 1,500 hovers, grouped by stack: (1) ~24,000 x 48-byte blocks, `rae_ext_rae_str_sub` <- String.trim <- treeRowLabelOf (inspectorSystem/NodeQuery.rae) <- collectTreeRows (recursive) <- syncTreePanel <- inspectorUpdate. The only trim on that path is `truncated(text:, limit:)` in NodeQuery.rae: `let flat: String = text.replace(old: "\n", new: " ").trim()` then `ret flat` or `ret "{flat.sub(start: 0, len: limit)}..."`. About 13 per refresh = the MainMenu Text nodes whose preview is cut with "...", so the evidence points at the TRUNCATING return path not dropping the owned local `flat` (verify: a Text short enough for `ret flat` should not leak). (2) ~1,900 x 16-byte blocks, `rae_ext_rae_str_interp` directly in syncTreePanel: `var header: String = "Hierarchy ({rows.length})"` (conditionally reassigned for the filter), then `chromeSystem.treeHeader = header`. Suspect this was INTRODUCED by 142db319 (#79484806, "`=` copies"): assigning a local into a field now deep-copies it, so the local must be dropped at scope end, and apparently is not for this `var` String; before that commit the store was a shallow alias and nothing leaked. Check by building the memory test with the compiler from 142db319^ vs 142db319. (3) ~800 x 32-byte `rae_string_copy` from listViewSystem -> mountSceneInstanceImpl -> StringMap.set: startup only (same count idle), ignore. Both real leaks look like COMPILER ownership bugs (an owned String local not dropped on some return path / after being copied into a field), not editor logic — fix them in the C backend, not by rewriting the editor code around them, and add a minimal fixture for each shape (String local returned through an interpolation on one path; `var s: String = interp`, conditional reassign, `field = s`) that asserts outstanding String allocations return to baseline, like fixture 918 does. WHY THE EXISTING GATE MISSED IT: run_examples.sh's hover-leak check (RAE_UI_EDITOR_TEST_HOVER_CYCLE=Title,Logo,600) calls the hover logic directly without painting and accepts up to 4 MB over 600 hovers; this leak is ~13 x 48 B + 16 B (~0.7 KB malloc) per refresh, ~0.4 MB per 600, under that threshold. HOW TO MEASURE: (a) `bash examples/121_ui_editor/tools/hover-memory-test.sh 20` (committed in 71647680) builds the editor, runs it headless with the test-only runtime hook RAE_GPU2D_TEST_POINTER="x1,y1,x2,y2,frames" (runtime_gpu2d_platform.c: the reported pointer alternates between two design-space points every N polls, driving the REAL frame loop; logs `[gpu2d-test-pointer] N moves, M painted frames` every 250 moves) plus RAE_MEM_STATS=1, samples RSS every 10 s and prints the mem:string:sub / interp / TOTAL / buf lines at exit. 20 s is enough: currently ~3,250 hovers leave ~45,000 sub and ~3,500 interp outstanding. Pass 600 for the full 10-minute run. (b) For call sites use a SEPARATE run WITHOUT RAE_MEM_STATS (its table of live-allocation pointers makes leaked blocks look referenced, so `leaks` reports nothing): build as the script does, run the app with RAE_UI_HEADLESS=1 RAE_SDL_HEADLESS_MS=40000 RAE_GPU2D_TEST_POINTER="623,196,787,297,1" MallocStackLogging=1 in the background, after ~20 s run `leaks <pid>` and read the `STACK OF N INSTANCES OF` groups. Idle baseline for `leaks` is ~116 blocks / ~0.8 MB (startup). DONE WHEN: the 20 s memory test shows string:sub and string:interp outstanding at the idle baseline (tens, not thousands) and flat with run length; `leaks` on the hover run matches the idle baseline; the two compiler fixtures pass and fail on the pre-fix compiler; and the run_examples.sh hover-leak gate is tightened to drive painted frames through RAE_GPU2D_TEST_POINTER and assert outstanding String counts (not a MB threshold), sabotage-checked. Full suite + 121 example gate green. — DONE: two COMPILER ownership bugs in c_stmt.c, both leaking an owned local, fixed at the root; the editor code is unchanged. Now emit_stmt saves x's moved bit before a `ret x` / `ret own x` and restores it after the statement, so the mark covers only that ret's own drop epilogue. (2) An ASSIGN pre-pass marked the identifier source of `target.field = local` moved (a leftover of when field stores moved), but every field store now COPIES an identifier source: String field (rae_string_copy), owned aggregate (#965 deep copy), and boxing into an optional field (rae_string_copy / rae_deep_copy into the box — the task's guess that the optional store moves was checked in the emitted C and is wrong). - [x] #39240138 {difficulty:4} [compiler/c_backend — a Rae identifier that is a C keyword emits invalid C] A local named `short` or `long` (`let short: String = ...`) is emitted verbatim as a C identifier: `rae_String short = ...` fails with "'short type-name' is invalid" and every use after it breaks. Found while writing a repro for the hover-leak task. Rae names should be free of C's reserved words: mangle (or prefix) any local/parameter/field name that collides with a C keyword or common macro (short, long, int, char, float, double, signed, unsigned, auto, register, volatile, const, static, extern, struct, union, enum, typedef, goto, default, sizeof, inline, restrict, _Bool…) consistently at declaration and every use, including struct fields, named-argument emission and generated helpers (toString/equals/toJson field names must still print the Rae name). Add a fixture that uses several such names as locals, params and fields. — DONE: one rename pass, not per-site mangling. compiler/src/c_names.c: c_rename_reserved_names runs at the start of c_backend_emit_module (after sema, so diagnostics keep the Rae spelling) and renames, in the AST, every local, parameter, field, call-argument label, struct-literal label, destructure/named-return label, query-loop binding, module-level let/const and member access spelled like a C11 keyword, a macro the generated C sees (bool true false NULL errno stdin stdout stderr EOF alignas alignof noreturn static_assert thread_local complex imaginary offsetof assert) or a libc function the generated code calls in a body (free malloc calloc realloc memcpy memmove memcmp memset strlen snprintf printf fprintf) to `<name>__kw` — declaration and every use together, so no emission site needs to know. Not renamed: function names and anything in callee position (keeps the `sizeof` intrinsic), type names, enum cases (already prefixed in C, e.g. JsonKind.bool; a `Kind.case` member is recognised and skipped) and c_struct fields. Text keeps the Rae spelling: struct toString builds its labels from rae_source_name (length-annotated literals); the toJson / fromJson block is emitted into a buffer and c_restore_names_in_literals strips the suffix inside C string literals only, so `this->short__kw` stays the C member while the key is "short"; fieldName() is folded by sema before the pass. The backend reads names only from the AST (TypeInfo links back to decls), so the rename is consistent. Cost: none measurable — UI editor emit 21.4 s before, 21.2 s after, and its emitted C is BYTE-IDENTICAL (the tree has no such names apart from the JsonKind.bool enum case). Fixture 922_c_keyword_names covers locals, params, named args, String/List/opt fields, a generic struct, a const, if let, a loop var, a StringMap local, struct printing, a toJson/fromJson round trip, fieldName via fields(), the JsonKind.bool enum case and libc-named locals; it fails to compile on the old compiler ('short type-name' is invalid) and passes now. Full suite 573/573. Version 0.1.83. Side findings filed as new tasks: a Rae keyword as a struct-literal key crashes the parser; interpolating a generic struct does not compile.
- [x] #55453128 {difficulty:4} [compiler/c_backend — a local moved to an own parameter only inside a branch is never freed when the branch is skipped] Found by the StringMap leak task (per-reload UI editor leak, 7 Strings per reload from examples/121_ui_editor/documentSystem/DocumentSystem.rae rebuildWatchedPaths: `let path: String = scenePackageFile(...)` then `if exists(path: path) { document.watchedPaths.add(value: path) }`). Minimal repro: `func maybeKeep(seed: view Int, keep: view Bool, into: mod List(String)) { let path: String = "path number {seed}"; if keep { into.add(value: path) } }` — 100 calls with keep=false leave +100 outstanding Strings (RAE_MEM_STATS, rae_ext_rae_mem_stats_outstanding), 0 expected. Cause: the call-argument move mark (c_call.c, mark_expr_moved_if_local for an own/consuming parameter) sets local_moved[] during emission and it stays set after the inner block, so the scope-exit drop is skipped on EVERY path, not just the one that moved. Same bug class as the `ret` fix in ed104aba (fixture 919), but a ret can restore the bit after its own statement; a call inside a branch cannot, because code after the branch runs on both paths. Needs a runtime live flag for a local moved on only some paths — the #885 machinery (local_drop_flag / `__rae_live_<name>`, today only for types with a user-written drop and only in the struct-drop branch of emit_implicit_drops_for_body) generalised to String / List / map / heap-struct locals, armed when a local is moved inside a nested block (a pre-scan like block_has_explicit_drop). Also check a move inside a loop body and inside a match arm. Add a fixture with the outstanding-allocation check (like 919/920/921) covering if / else / loop / match, and verify with 30 reloads of the editor (touch the scene under a headless editor with RAE_MEM_STATS=1: outstanding Strings should stop growing by 7 per reload). — DONE: a local moved on SOME paths only now carries a runtime live flag. At its `let`, a pre-scan of the rest of the block (c_stmt.c rest_moves_name_conditionally) arms `int __rae_live_<name> = 1` for a heap-owning local that is passed as a call argument (bare or `own x`) inside an if / else / loop / match / defer body, a loop condition or step, a match arm, or the right of and/or — over-reporting is safe, the flag only guards the drop. The two move sites that can clear it in place do: a bare local into a consuming call parameter (c_call.c) and an `own x` expression (c_expr.c) emit `(__rae_live_x = 0, x)`, so the flag clears exactly when that argument is evaluated. Every other move site still sets the compile-time mark, unchanged (a first version skipped the mark for flagged locals and double-freed the UI editor's createApp: a bare local in a `ret App { ... }` literal is moved by the mark, not by an instrumented site). Scope-exit drops (emit_implicit_drops_for_body, also used by ret/break epilogues) are now guarded by the flag for EVERY type — the per-local drop moved into emit_local_drop; before, the #885 guard existed only for structs with a user drop. Reassignment guards the old value too: a String local's reassign no longer frees a value that was moved away (skipped when marked moved, `if (__rae_live_x)` when flagged, then the flag is re-armed), and the aggregate reassign guards release_old the same way. Fixture 923_conditional_move_releases_other_paths runs every shape both ways — a String moved in if / else / a match arm / the right of and, a struct declared in a loop body and moved on one iteration, `own` of a List in an if, a String reassigned after a conditional move and after an unconditional one — and checks the values that arrive and 0 outstanding allocations; the previous compiler's binary exits 1 without output. (A move inside a loop followed by break is rejected by sema as use-after-move; not changed here.) UI editor, 30 scene reloads (headless, touching the scene, RAE_MEM_STATS=1): outstanding Strings 24 -> 248 before (8 per reload), 3 -> 31 now (1 per reload); buffers 3 -> 31, 1 per reload. The remaining String + buffer per reload is the List temporary of #34355043 (sceneImports(...) in a condition whose body returns) and its one item. Full suite 574/574; full example gate 77/77 (121 and 106 included). Version 0.1.84.
- [x] #34355043 {difficulty:4} [compiler/c_backend — a `ret` inside an if body skips freeing the condition's hoisted temporaries] Found by the StringMap leak task (per-reload UI editor leak, 1 List buffer per reload from examples/121_ui_editor/documentSystem/DocumentSystem.rae reportUnimportedTheme: `if sceneImports(scene: document.scene).length > 0 or sceneDeclaresTokens(...) { ret }`). Minimal repro: `func check(count: view Int) ret Int { if makeList(count: count).length > 0 or other() { ret 1 }; ret 0 }` with makeList returning a List(String) — 100 calls leave +100 buffers and +200 Strings (the list and its items); the same condition WITHOUT a ret in the body frees everything. Add a fixture with the outstanding-allocation check (ret / break / continue inside an if and a loop whose condition holds a heap temporary), and verify with 30 editor reloads (outstanding buffers should stop growing by 1 per reload). — DONE: the ret epilogue (c_stmt.c, AST_STMT_RET) now also drops the temporaries of every statement the ret sits in: after emit_stmt_temp_drops_now (its own statement's temps) it walks ctx->stmt_temps->parent to the root with emit_stmt_temp_drops_chain(ctx, out, NULL). Each drop is guarded by its `_set` flag and clears it, so the enclosing statement's own drop after the whole if stays a no-op on this path. The return value is computed (and copied where it must be) before any drop, so nothing it returns can dangle. break / continue already walked the chain up to the loop (#886); verified, not changed. Fixture 924_ret_frees_enclosing_temporaries: the editor's shape (temporary in an `or` condition, ret in the body), a ret two statements deep (an if temp inside a loop whose condition also holds one), a ret whose value is built from a second temporary, and break / continue inside ifs with heap temporaries — each both ways, values checked, 0 outstanding; 450 leaked on the previous compiler. UI editor, 30 scene reloads (headless, RAE_MEM_STATS=1): outstanding Strings 0 and buffers 0, idle and after 30 reloads (before this task: +1 String and +1 buffer per reload; before the two earlier reload tasks: +8 Strings +1 buffer). Also fixed, found on the way: register_generic_type (c_backend.c) looked up a struct by name and could take an already SPECIALISED copy (Pair(Pair(Int))), whose fields are concrete; substituting into it for Pair(Int) gave Pair(Int) back, and an already-registered type rescans its fields, so a nested generic next to a List(Pair(Int)) crashed the COMPILER with a stack overflow (3-line repro; pre-existing, the unchanged compiler crashes too). It now takes the generic template. Label: a generic instance prints its base name, `Pair { first: 1, second: 2 }`, like the bare-brace literal that builds it. An `opt Pair(Int)` field serializes as null, exactly like an opt of a non-generic struct (no scalar JSON form) — unchanged. Fixture 926_generic_struct_helpers: interpolation of Pair(Int)/Pair(String)/Pair(Pair(Int)), toString(), a List(Pair(Int)), formatting inside a function generic over T, equals by content (equal and unequal Pair(String), nested), a struct with a Pair(Int) and a List(Pair(Int)) field round-tripped through toJson/fromJson and compared equal, Pair(Int).fromJson, and 0 outstanding allocations; the previous compiler crashes on it. Full suite 577/577, full example gate 77/77. Version 0.1.87. Side finding filed below: a nested bare-brace literal for a nested generic types its second field wrong.
- [x] #57294594 {difficulty:4} [compiler/c_backend — a collection loop over a call result never frees the collection] `loop let item: view String in makeList(count: 3) { ... }` (makeList returns a List(String)) emits `rae_List_rae_String __rae_collection0 = rae_Main_makeList_...(count);` and a for over it, and nothing ever drops `__rae_collection0`: 100 calls leak ~300 Strings plus the list buffers whether the loop runs to the end or returns out of its body (measured with RAE_MEM_STATS / rae_ext_rae_mem_stats_outstanding, found while testing the ret-temporaries fix). Only an iterable that is a NEW value (a call, a literal) is owned by the loop; an iterable that names a place (`in items`, `in world.rows`) must stay a borrow and must not be dropped. Fix: when the iterable is a new value, drop `__rae_collection<N>` after the loop, and on every exit from it (ret inside the body, break — check continue does not), guarded by a set flag like the statement temporaries (register it as one, or reuse emit_stmt_temp_drops_chain). Fixture with the outstanding-allocation check (loop to the end, break, ret out of the body, nested loops) and a place iterable that must NOT be dropped (its list still readable after the loop). — DONE (compiler/src/c_stmt.c emit_loop, collection form): a collection loop whose iterable is a NEW value (a call or method call, e.g. `in makeList()`, `in text.split(sep:)`) now owns the collection. It gets its own statement-temporary layer, a CStmtTemps holding `if (__rae_collection<N>_set) { ... drop ... }`, linked ABOVE the loop statement's own temporaries for the duration of the body: a `ret` in the body walks the whole chain (the #34355043 epilogue) and releases it; break / continue stop at the loop's own temporaries (loop_temps) and leave it — continue still iterates it, and after a break the drop at the end of the loop runs; the end of the loop drops it once. An iterable that names a PLACE (an ident, a member, an index: `in items`, `in holder.items`, `in xs[i]`), a view/mod iterable, and an Array(T, cap:) are borrowed and never dropped, as before. (A list LITERAL cannot be an iterable — sema requires a List/Array expression — so it needs no case.) Fixture 927_loop_owns_new_collection: to the end, break, continue (skips the first item and reads the next two intact), ret out of the body, nested loops each over a new list, two method-call iterables (String.split), and three borrowed iterables (a local, a field, a view parameter) still intact after their loops — values checked, 0 outstanding; 900 leaked on the previous compiler. Recommend: make it an error (a small sema check next to the view->mod one), since `own` there asserts a move that does not happen. QUESTION: for each of (1) fix-to-copy, (2) correct the table to error OR make the compiler copy, (3) make it an error — which do you want? ANSWERED 2026-09-30 and DONE: (1) fix to deep-copy, (2) copy — recommended for consistency with (1): the table's row is "alias or field", an alias is only another name for the field, and the error's `"{...}"` escape only works for Strings — (3) make it an error. Codegen (c_call.c own_takes_copy): an `own` parameter handed a PLACE — a field, an element, a view/mod alias or parameter, or a global — goes through the existing `copy T` deep-copy path; a bare owned local still moves, a fresh value is taken, `own x` is the explicit move. The backend's borrowed-argument error (#363) and sema's "does not own its value" error are retired (the value is copied now), and sema no longer counts an alias passed to `own` as moved. Sema: `own x` into a `copy` parameter is an error naming both ("'own name' moves, but parameter 'text' is 'copy' ...").
